title: The backlog gate prints its JSON verdict for non-merge checks
description:

Plain mode exposed the actual time-span-unreceipted finding, which is repaired separately. Source non-merge main path invokes judged(..., json), but judged only prints stdout when !json and main never forwards r.stdout for this path. Merge mode forwards mg.stdout. No product/native acceptance failure is implied.

DONE WHEN: the documented npm run backlog:json/non-merge gate emits its complete parseable JSON result on stdout for both green and red verdicts, preserving correct exit0/1/2 and useful stderr. Add isolated CLI regression coverage for non-merge green/red and preserve merge output. Do not edit maintained gate copies by hand; route the correction through the skills/setup integration and normal version checks.

Lane: deferred tooling/check-output debt; no finding budget spend or current milestone expansion. This is a fault in maintained check wiring, not an instance feature requirement. Plain gate remains usable, so it does not block the validated q4x merge. No external skill issue is sent without owner approval.

title: Modules get their credentials from OpenBao, and only the egress gateway reaches the world
description:
Outcome 5, feature 4 of 7. ADR-010 Q7 / Q5 networks: per-process OpenBao roles delivered by the Bank-Vaults secrets webhook (vault-env daemon mode), default-deny NetworkPolicy, the egress gateway as the only route out with Agent Vault injecting the model key, RBAC with no Docker anywhere, Motor's sandbox Jobs constrained. Re-walks outcome 4's 'no key in lifemodel's process'. Checks Q8, Q9, N-7..N-11, N-18.

## DONE WHEN
No module pod spec, environment, file or log holds the model key or a store credential; a module pod cannot reach any outside address directly, and its model request reaches the stub endpoint through the egress gateway with the key injected by Agent Vault.

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-10-15 (lifemodel-vhd design, ADR-011 D5): the web module (Deployment `web` in `lifemodel`) runs on the core's store credentials until this feature. This feature must give it its own identity in target form: its service account -> an OpenBao role -> leased credentials scoped to the intake script on `inbound` and its receipts (`inbound:receipt:*`), reading `outbound` as a hint, reading the creature-state key, and SELECT on core.conversation_messages. ADR-011 "Amendments to ADR-010" updates the Q7 matrix row for the web module accordingly.

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text:
Owner decisions, 2026-10-16 (conversation on how lifemodel survives a broken model client or a provider change):
- Model access is configured in the loader at first start, beside the password, not in lifemodel's settings: a primary endpoint with its key, and a reserve endpoint. Kept in OpenBao; lifemodel never sees the keys. lifemodel's own settings keep only the choice of model per role (fast, smart), which the generation check validates.
- Endpoint kinds: OpenAI-compatible APIs (the owner's own gateway, OpenRouter) and Ollama (through its OpenAI-compatible `/v1` API), local or in-cluster. A local Ollama as the reserve is the last line that depends on no provider and no Internet.
- The egress gateway stays thin: it injects the key, lets requests out only to the configured endpoints (a local-network Ollama is its own explicit allowance), and switches to the reserve when the primary does not answer or answers with a protocol error. It does not translate provider protocols; no LiteLLM inside the instance (an OpenAI-compatible intermediary outside does that job).
- "No connection to the model since HH:MM, error …" is a health signal that needs no model: shown in the web interface's "Сейчас" panel and in the loader.
The core keeps one endpoint in code (AGENTS.md "no separate keyed provider and no fallback"): the reserve lives in the gateway, not in the core.

title: The loader has its own interface on the kit: a setup wizard with onboarding on first start, then settings
description:
Charter instance-1, outcomes 4 and 5. Design: ADR-012 (`docs/adr/012-loader-interface-and-access.md`), owner decisions of 2026-10-15/16 (comments below). The target story the owner tests, together with lifemodel-2t5 (owner 2026-10-16: "доработай все сразу … потом буду тестировать целевую историю"; both features before the test): one installer command → it prints `https://lifemodel.local/` and the CA fingerprint → from another LAN computer the browser opens it by mDNS over HTTPS → a first-start wizard on the kit (onboarding, password, model access checked with a real request, this device) → the chat. Afterwards settings, never the wizard again.

The loader's interface is the same React + shadcn/ui kit and theme as the chat (ADR-011 D8), static files baked into the loader image — never from a generation. Model access: primary and optional reserve endpoint, OpenAI-compatible or Ollama `/v1`, keys to OpenBao only.

Out: own domain / Let's Encrypt (lifemodel-sd2), generations/rollback pages (their features), lifemodel's own settings, Android without mDNS.

## DONE WHEN
On the test VM from a clean snapshot, installed with one command, from another LAN machine in real Chromium and Firefox: `http://lifemodel.local/` redirects to `https://lifemodel.local/`, the served certificate chains to the instance CA whose fingerprint the installer printed; the wizard (onboarding, password, model access against a stub endpoint and a made-up key, each checked; this device with the CA download) lands logged in on the loader and "Open the chat" reaches the chat without a second password; the key is in OpenBao and in no file, log, page or API response; a second visit shows settings, not the wizard; a changed endpoint is checked and saved; the password change works; no cookie carries `Domain`, all carry `Secure`; the pages are built only from kit components (provenance check), in both themes and both languages, and pass axe-core; with lifemodel's generation broken the loader pages still load.
close_reason: accepted at 1ca860e: owner's combined test 2026-10-19 on a fresh VM ('в целом все ок', closing agreed 'В целом да'); VM walk record on lifemodel-s9v5.2; acceptance record on the stage; CI green; feature criterion met (the owner set up the instance and talked to lifemodel through the web interface with their own model); deferred by the owner: design pass lifemodel-bnhq, acquaintance lifemodel-w3s3

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text:
Owner decision 2026-10-16 — how the owner reaches the loader and the app (replaces the `*.localhost` + SSH tunnel used on the test VM):

- In the home network the instance is reached by an mDNS name the node announces itself (e.g. `http://lifemodel.local/`, loader at `boot.lifemodel.local`); the installer ends by printing that address. Plain HTTP, LAN only.
- First-start setup is open from the LAN without a one-time code or password ("так тоже часто делают"); once the password is set, login is required as today. Risk accepted by the owner: whoever on the LAN opens setup first sets the password.
- HTTPS is offered by binding the owner's own domain with a Let's Encrypt certificate (DNS-01, no inbound ports) — lifemodel-sd2. The wizard offers it; without it, access stays LAN-only HTTP and the PWA cannot be installed (secure context required).
- Tailscale is rejected: it is blocked for the owner. Because a domain allows wildcard names, the separate `boot.` host (origin isolation of the loader from the app) is kept.

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text:
Owner decision 2026-10-16 (amends the decision above: "HTTPS by default, as Proxmox does"):

- The installer creates the instance's own certificate authority and issues from it a server certificate for `lifemodel.local` and `boot.lifemodel.local`. The instance serves HTTPS from the first start; plain HTTP only redirects to HTTPS. LAN traffic, the setup wizard included, is never sent in clear.
- The installer ends by printing the address and the certificate's fingerprint, so the owner can check the browser's warning is for their own node.
- The loader offers the root certificate for download as an optional step. Installed on a device, it removes the warning and makes the PWA installable without a domain.
- Binding the owner's domain with Let's Encrypt (lifemodel-sd2) replaces this certificate; access from outside the LAN still needs the domain.

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text:
Owner decision 2026-10-16 — scope added to this feature: the installer is the first screen of the onboarding.

- The loader, not the installer, creates the instance's certificate authority and the server certificate at first start, and keeps the CA key with the other secrets in the cluster. The NixOS module and scripts/install.sh therefore stay equivalent.
- Both installers end for a person, not an engineer: they wait until the loader answers, then print `https://lifemodel.local/` and the certificate fingerprint. When something did not come up they say what, and point to `lifemodel doctor`.
- Installation is one line without required engineering parameters: the platform URL and version default to the latest signed release.
- Today they need --platform-url and --tag/--digest, print only "done (k3s …, Flux …, platform source applied)", and do not wait for the loader.

Unit/integration tests: host lists and Origin derive from the configured name and refuse `localhost`; the loader creates the CA and server certificate once (idempotent across restarts, renewed when 30 days remain, SANs = the three names); every Set-Cookie has `Secure` and no `Domain`. `nix flake check` renders the substituted Ingress and the avahi/firewall units. After the fix all three units active; a capture on the VM shows A queries from the dev machine (192.168.0.25) answered "A 192.168.0.122" for lifemodel.local, boot-lifemodel.local, vault-lifemodel.local; an unknown name is not answered. Firewall: TCP 80/443 and UDP 5353 admitted only on ens18 (iptables nixos-fw). Avahi effective config: allow-interfaces=ens18, publishing on.

Both engines.
- DEFECT (goes with lifemodel-3wi9.4.1, which replaces these forms): first visit with no password goes login?next → /setup and drops next, so after setup the browser stays on boot-lifemodel.local/ instead of the chat. Handed to the 4.1 worker with a test requirement; re-walked at the 4.x walk.

title: The instance's name reaches the platform and the application through one substituted Kustomization, and every host is <name>.local or boot-<name>.local
description:
ADR-012 Decision 1 (and the routing half of Decision 4). Instance name (default `lifemodel`, one DNS label ≤ 57 chars, fixed after install): `services.lifemodel.name` / `install.sh --name` write `flux-system/lifemodel-instance` before the root Kustomization; a new `platform-instance` Kustomization (path `./instance`, the ONLY one with `postBuild.substituteFrom`, `optional: false`, ordered by `dependsOn`) carries the namespace-local ConfigMaps `lifemodel-instance` in `lifemodel-system` and `lifemodel` and every public Ingress/Middleware (moved out of a0/a). Hosts `<name>.local`, `boot-<name>.local`, `vault-<name>.local`; `boot-` routes entirely to the loader without ForwardAuth; the app host keeps ForwardAuth except exact `/_auth/handoff` → loader. Loader and web read `LIFEMODEL_NAME` via `configMapKeyRef`; hosts/origins/redirects derive from it (HTTP scheme still — HTTPS is lifemodel-3wi9.3.4); the web module serves `GET /api/instance` and the chat reads the loader address from it (no literal links). The loader answers 404 for paths not in ADR-012's route table on each host. `*.localhost` removed everywhere (code, tests, docs).
## DONE WHEN
Tests: a Flux-equivalent post-build render of `platform-instance` for names `lifemodel` and `home` changes only intended fields, leaves no placeholder, and the OpenBao/Gitea manifests are byte-identical; a missing ConfigMap fails; a bad/too-long name fails `nix flake check` and `install.sh`; the loader answers `boot-lifemodel.local`, refuses `boot.localhost`/`localhost`; `/_auth/handoff` is answered only on the app host; the web module's Origin and `/api/instance` follow the name; the chat's loader link comes from `/api/instance`. Normally the full check is green.

title: The loader issues the instance CA into its own volume and the server certificate into the precreated TLS Secret before it serves anything, and renews it
description:
ADR-012 Decision 3. Before opening HTTP the loader runs the certificate bootstrap with A0 resources only: CA key in `/var/lib/loader/pki/ca.key` (0600, never a Secret), instance identity `/var/lib/loader/instance.json` (CA fingerprint) written after the CA is read back, leaf into the A0-precreated Secret `lifemodel-system/lifemodel-tls` (IfNotPresent, prune disabled; loader get/update on that name only), CA certificate in ConfigMap `lifemodel-system/lifemodel-ca`; readiness only after the leaf is in place. Missing/expiring leaf reissued from the same CA (start + daily timer, 30 days before expiry of 397); missing/corrupt CA with an identity → visible failure, doctor reports it. X.509 profile as ADR-012 (P-256, CA pathlen 0 keyCertSign/cRLSign; leaf SANs = three names, serverAuth; random serials; notBefore −1 h) with pinned `@peculiar/x509`. Loader Deployment strategy `Recreate`. `GET /ca.crt` on `boot-` serves the CA certificate.
## DONE WHEN
Tests (fake k8s API, injected clock): first start creates CA → identity → leaf in that order and only then reports ready; restart reuses; deleted leaf reissued with the same CA; deleted CA with identity fails; the timer renews at 30 days; profile fields parsed and asserted; RBAC manifests give the loader get/update on `lifemodel-tls` only and no Secret create; `/ca.crt` returns the PEM. Normally the full check is green.

title: The loader checks a model endpoint safely and saves it to OpenBao in the same request, under its own Bao policy and a narrow egress rule
description:
ADR-012 Decision 7 (backend only; the wizard UI is lifemodel-3wi9.4.3). An initial bootstrap phase (before root retirement; clean installs only) mounts KV v2 at `lifemodel/` and binds policy `loader-model` (create/update/read `lifemodel/data/model/*`, read `lifemodel/metadata/model/*`) to the loader's Kubernetes-auth role; the loader re-logs in on token expiry; sealed/unreachable Bao → 503. The safe checker: https public or http/https RFC 1918 (LAN Ollama); refuses URL credentials, other schemes, loopback, link-local/metadata, pod/service CIDRs, IPv6/mapped literals of those, and names resolving to them; resolves once and connects to the validated address with SNI = original host; no redirects; 15 s and 64 KiB bound; one check per slot. `PUT /api/model/<primary|reserve>` checks and saves in one request (omitted key = keep stored key; new key replaces); `DELETE /api/model/reserve`; `GET /api/model` returns `keySet` only. Safe error codes only; no key, upstream body or query URL in any log. Loader NetworkPolicy egress gains `0.0.0.0/0` except pod/service CIDRs and `169.254.0.0/16`; ADR-010's loader egress row amended. `onboarding.json` advances to the device step only after the primary is saved.
## DONE WHEN
Tests: rebinding, redirect-to-private, IPv6/mapped literals, metadata, slow and oversized bodies refused; LAN Ollama without key accepted; an endpoint echoing the key on success and error never leaks it to a response or a recording logger; a PUT whose check fails saves nothing; keep/replace/clear semantics; Bao 503 when sealed; the bootstrap phase's policy text and role binding asserted; the NetworkPolicy render asserted. Normally the full check is green.

title: The installer ends by printing the address and the certificate fingerprint
description:
Stage 4 of lifemodel-3wi9. ADR-012 Decision 6: one installer line with no required parameters (platform URL and tag default to the latest signed release; `--name` optional); the installer waits up to 10 min for `https://boot-<name>.local/` from the node, then prints the address and the CA fingerprint, or on timeout names the step that is not ready and points to `lifemodel doctor`; `lifemodel address` prints the same at any time; the NixOS bootstrap unit logs it.

## DONE WHEN
Installer tests (render-only and a faked cluster): defaults resolve to the release URL/tag; the wait times out with the step named; the printed fingerprint equals the DER SHA-256 of the CA certificate in ConfigMap `lifemodel-ca`. `nix flake check` passes. On the test VM, `lifemodel address` prints `https://lifemodel.local/` and the fingerprint that the browser shows for the CA.

title: The installer runs with no required parameters from a pinned release and ends by printing the address and the CA fingerprint
description:
ADR-012 Decision 8. The release workflow stamps `install.sh` and the flake's module default with the release's platform URL and digest; the installer downloaded from the latest GitHub release needs no parameters (`--name`, `--lan-interface` optional; existing flags kept) and persists name + digest in `/etc/lifemodel/instance.env` (rerun keeps them unless another release is passed explicitly; another name is refused). After applying it waits ≤ 10 min (each request ≤ 10 s) for anonymous `GET https://boot-<name>.local/api/state` = 200 via `--resolve` to 127.0.0.1 with `--cacert` from ConfigMap `lifemodel-ca` (no `-k`), then prints the address and "SHA-256 fingerprint of the CA certificate (DER)"; on timeout names the first not-ready step and points to `lifemodel doctor`. `lifemodel address` prints the same from the established identity, distinguishes not installed / not ready, never reads the CA key; the NixOS bootstrap unit logs it.
## DONE WHEN
Installer tests on a faked cluster: the stamped defaults; persisted name/digest across a rerun; another name refused; the wait succeeds on 200 with the right CA and fails on a wrong certificate, 401/5xx and timeout with the step named; the printed fingerprint equals the DER SHA-256 of the ConfigMap's CA. CLI test for `lifemodel address`. `nix flake check` green. Normally the full check is green.

comments.text: Design confirmation round (ADR12-C-06): the release workflow publishes, after pushing and verifying the signed platform, a versioned installer bundle (install.sh + root templates + CLI, platform URL and digest stamped) as a GitHub release asset; the release job gains `contents: write` only; a clean-directory smoke run of the downloaded bundle. NixOS module default: the platform tag of the flake's own version (signature identity pinned), evaluation offline. Do not try to embed the platform's digest into bytes the platform itself contains.

title: A model slot carries custom upstream headers, with {session} filled from the caller's conversation, so an endpoint that needs x-opencode-session works
description:
Owner 2026-10-19: "Еще нужна возможность задать произвольные заголовки. Сейчас с opencode go модель не может работать, ей нужен: x-opencode-session"; value: a template with the conversation id ("Шаблон с ID разговора"), as the owner's pi gateway sends the current session id in x-opencode-session. Finding 1 of 8 in motor-1 (tasks will use the same gateway); taken first, before lifemodel-5f4q.

What a person does: saves an opencode go endpoint as a slot. What happens: the upstream refuses requests without x-opencode-session. Expected: the slot holds custom headers (stored with the slot in OpenBao, treated as secret like the key), the gateway adds them upstream, and a value containing {session} gets the session id the core passes for its conversation (each future task its own).

Criterion: a slot saved with header x-opencode-session: {session} makes the gateway send that header with the core's conversation id to the upstream, and the loader's check sends it with a probe id; reserved or hop-by-hop names (authorization, host, content-length, connection and the like) and values with CR/LF are refused at save; header values never appear in /status, logs, the core or responses; a slot without headers behaves as before.
close_reason: Accepted on d10a098 (PR #75)

title: A turn that failed during a model outage is answered once the model is back, without waiting for a core restart
description:
Final walk 2026-10-19: with both model slots down the owner's message failed ('Inbound turn failed; its messages remain pending for bounded retry'); after the primary came back it stayed unanswered, because the retry of a failed inbound turn happens only in a fresh core (AGENTS.md Restart guarantees). The owner sees only the outage line. Owner: 'Эту веху не нужно расширять' -> deferred, not instance-1.
Wanted: a model-unavailable failure is retried in the running core when the gateway reports recovery (bounded), keeping the two-attempt/error-notice rule for other failures.

title: A web rollout drains the old pod before it stops, so Traefik never answers 502 during it
description:
Found by the lifemodel-vhd acceptance walk (2026-10-16): right after a web rollout (maxSurge 1 / maxUnavailable 0) one request through Traefik got 502 while the old pod terminated — Traefik still routed to it for a moment; 200 again within 3 s. Intake is not lost (the tab retries with the same id, ADR-011 Decision 2), but ADR-011 Decision 3 means intake to stay available through web rollouts.

## DONE WHEN
The web Deployment drains before stopping (a preStop delay longer than the endpoint propagation, with a termination grace period above it, and the server closing its listener and streams after it), and on the test VM a web rollout under a request every 200 ms through Traefik shows no 502/503; normally a rollout still completes within its usual time.

title: CI builds and renders what is deployed, so a broken loader image or platform render cannot merge green
description:
Owner decisions 2026-10-19: 'Назначь в следующую веху' (deferred out of instance-1, finding budget spent), then at the instance-1 retrospective (lifemodel-vz26) 'Да, принимаю': lut.3.6 joins this feature, and CI may gain a Nix job for the platform render; placed first in the milestone that follows instance-1.

Why: #67 merged green while the loader image no longer built (fixed in #68; loader-ui-build.test.ts catches only that one case); review finding L-06: the real Kustomize render of deploy/platform runs only in nix flake check, which CI does not run. CI builds the core and web images only.

## DONE WHEN
On every PR whose changes reach them: a ci-loader-image job runs scripts/release/prepare-loader-context.sh and builds docker/loader/Dockerfile; a job with Nix (pinned action, read-only permissions) runs nix flake check including the platform render. A planted break (a removed COPY; a missing resource reference) fails the PR, and normally such a PR goes green.

Left out: publishing the loader image from CI.

title: CI builds the loader image on every PR that reaches it, so a broken loader Dockerfile cannot merge green
description:
A ci-loader-image job in .github/workflows/ci.yml, gated by the changes filter like ci-core-image and ci-web-image, runs scripts/release/prepare-loader-context.sh and builds docker/loader/Dockerfile (no push). prepare-loader-context.sh requires non-zero core and web digests in the committed tree; the job must satisfy that without publishing (e.g. use the committed pins, or a documented CI-only path), never by weakening the script for releases.

## DONE WHEN
A PR that removes a COPY the loader image needs fails ci-loader-image; normally a PR touching loader/ goes green. Publishing the loader image from CI is left out.

title: The web provenance check runs when CI cannot read the changed paths, instead of being skipped
description:
Found in the review of lifemodel-5f4q.1 (PR #81). When the changes job cannot read the merge base, its fallback answers product=true with no changed-path records; scripts/ci-web-provenance-paths.sh counts only records and answers web_app=false, so ci-shadcn-provenance is skipped exactly when nothing is known. Reproduce: printf "product=true\n" | sh scripts/ci-web-provenance-paths.sh prints web_app=false. Fix as in ci-loader-paths.sh: no records selects the check, with a test tying the real workflow fallback to the selector.

## DONE WHEN
The fallback output (product=true, no records) makes ci-web-provenance-paths.sh print web_app=true, pinned by a test that runs the real producer and selector; a docs-only change still prints web_app=false.

title: A file-size ratchet stops any source or test file from growing past its recorded size, and new files from passing about 800 lines
description:
Owner 2026-10-19: "В следующую и только как храповик" — for the next milestone (generations-1), and only as a ratchet. Why: files grow because workers add code and tests to the existing file of the same topic and nothing stops them (core-loop.ts 2804 lines, calories-tool.ts 2600, loader-http-auth.test.ts 2283, plugin-loader.ts 2060, model-gateway.test.ts 1925).

A ratchet, not a cleanup: no file is split by this task. A size limit (about 800 lines, ESLint max-lines or a small check script) covers src/, loader/, web/ and tests/. Every file over it today is listed in a committed baseline with its current line count. A new file over the limit, or a listed file growing past its recorded count, fails the check in CI and in `npm run check`. A listed file that shrinks lowers its recorded count; one that falls under the limit leaves the list. The list can only shrink.

## DONE WHEN
A PR that adds a new 900-line file, or adds lines to a listed file beyond its recorded count, fails a required CI check; and normally a PR that shrinks or keeps a listed file goes green and lowers its recorded count.

Left out: splitting the existing large files (each is split when work touches it, as its own task).

title: Each task runs in its own container: a Kubernetes Job with a replaceable agent from one workbench image, its own files, no keys
description:
Charter motor-1, outcome 2 (agreed 2026-10-19). Was instance-1 outcome 6 'Tasks run in parallel, each within its own limits'; its Agent Vault/Landlock/uid shape is replaced by the owner's decisions recorded in the comments (2026-10-13, 2026-10-14, 2026-10-19).

The core starts each task as its own Kubernetes Job behind an executor seam (first implementation: plain Jobs; SkyPilot a later backend, lifemodel-zn55). Inside runs an agent harness behind its own seam (prime-agent one candidate; others, e.g. a DeepSeek harness, compared in research before the design). One workbench image (agent, git, node, build tools, lifemodel's dev dependencies), built, signed and pinned in the platform release by CI until the generation operator exists. Each task has its own working volume, reaches the model only through the model gateway, holds no key, and is removed when it ends. Its output (log and result) and the files it marks as artifacts outlive it, in S3-compatible object storage inside the cluster (not MinIO, archived 2026-04-25); the task holds no storage key either.

## DONE WHEN
On the test VM, two tasks started from the core run at once as separate Jobs with different profiles; each sees only its own files; neither has a key in its spec, environment, files or logs; each reaches the model through the gateway and nothing else unless its profile allows it; a task ended or stopped leaves no pod or working volume behind, while its output and the files it marked as artifacts remain: the agent reads them and the owner sees and downloads them in the task's panel. Swapping the harness or the executor implementation changes no caller of the seams (a second fake implementation passes the same contract tests).

comments.text:
Design frame for lifemodel-653 confirmed by the owner 2026-10-20 ('Да'), after two rounds on the target flow.

Target flow: owner asks -> the agent replies at once and creates a task with a briefing and a profile it sets (network allow-list or none, CPU/memory, timeout) within the owner's ceilings (beyond them: asks the owner) -> queued if the concurrency setting is reached, else started as a Kubernetes Job with the harness chosen in settings (OpenCode or prime-agent) -> the agent and the task talk live (task reports steps, findings, questions; the agent steers and checks the task does what the owner asked; the owner never writes to a task) -> before any change outside the task's working volume (push/PR, deploy, publish, grant a secret or network, change settings) the agent asks the owner for one exact scoped action; for dangerous or irreversible actions (a configurable list) the owner must write in words exactly what they allow, and only that is granted; enforced by the platform granting the specific access only after consent; secrets never pass the chat (the owner puts them in OpenBao) -> on end the task's result, log and marked files go to SeaweedFS; container and working volume are removed -> the agent replies with a summary and attachments -> results kept 90 days / forever / pinned, 20 GB ceiling, one batched warning before deletion. Stop, failure (with reason) and a core restart lose neither status nor result.

Outcome: the owner hands long work to the agent and keeps talking; results persist for the owner and the agent.
Drivers, most important first: isolation (own files, no key, model only via the gateway); nothing lost (core restart, stop, failure); nothing without consent (platform-enforced, exact scope); the agent steers the task live; replaceable harness and executor seams; limits from settings enforced by the platform; visible progress (step line, log, status).
Constraints: single-node k3s; default-deny network; task registry in Postgres; one workbench image built by CI.
Placement: 653 = launch by agent-set profile, live agent<->task channel, artifacts store, queue, settings registry (first step); ey3e = ceilings, access requests, consent gate and grants, secrets via OpenBao; hf2k = panel and task card UI; 97bj = old Motor Cortex removal.

comments.author: claude-code-coordinator
comments.text:
Every command reads the adapter's export: --backlog <path | ->. Commands that write print the
records to post, each under the item it goes on; post each body exactly as printed.

runs.mjs claim --item <id> --role coordinator|worker|agent [--forecast phase=min,...] [--away <min> | --due <time>]
                [--tasks N] [--stages N] [--basis <text>] [--note <text>]
  the claim that starts a span; first, the receipt of this session's open span on another item
runs.mjs claim --recovered --item <id> --role <role> --harness <h> --session <id> --at <time> [--basis <record>] [--note <text>]
  the claim another session made and never wrote, at the start its transcript here shows; then gaps.
  Where no machine has the transcript, at the start the record named in --basis shows; then receipt --unknown
runs.mjs claim --claims-for <harness:session> --item <id> --role <role> [--forecast ...] [--away <min> | --due <time>] [--tasks N] [--stages N] [--note <text>]
  the claim for a run this session is starting in another session, which cannot claim yet: the span is the run's (its key), this
  session's key is kept in the record, and the run claims nothing again -- its receipt ends the span
runs.mjs receipt [--span <id>] --end paused|finished|handed-over|stopped [--reason owner|missing|other] [--note <text>] [--recovered]
  what the span spent, measured from this machine's transcript (exit 3 when it is not here)
runs.mjs receipt --span <id> --end ... --unknown --note <why>
  closes a span whose transcript no machine has: its time unknown, the reason said
runs.mjs event [--span <id>] --event stop|decision|ci [--reason owner|missing|other] [--note <text>]
runs.mjs exec --item <id> --backlog <path | -> [--first <minutes>] -- <command and its arguments>
  runs one long command (a test, a check, a build) under the bound of the same command's own
  recorded durations: their longest, never below 10 s; with nothing recorded, the estimate --first
  names before the first run, or the first-run default (15 min) -- a guess said first, never a
  bound raised after a failure. Past the bound the command is stopped (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) and
  the exit is 124; a run it stopped loosens no bound. The duration record prints like the others,
  and the next run of the same command reads its bound from it.
runs.mjs finish --item <feature> --result pull-request|abandoned|stopped [--pr <url>] [--note <text>]
  this session's receipt, then the feature's summary: forecast against work by phase, occupied time
runs.mjs recovery --item <id> --grade R0|R1|R2|R3 [--from <harness>] [--to <harness>] [--note <text>]
runs.mjs void --comment <id> --note <why>
  retires a damaged or wrong record, which a tracker cannot delete; a correction then writes the right one
runs.mjs notify --note "<one line>" --config <gate config>
  one line through the owner's own channel ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shady2k-skills/notify.json, the
  command as {"command": [program, ...args]}, the line as the last argument); says plainly when none
  is set, that the project records no pushes, or that a send failed. The gate config is required:
  what it records about the pushes is the consent, and nothing is sent without saying it
runs.mjs progress --item <feature|milestone> [--no-transcripts] [--target <date>]
  where the work stands as the records hold it: earned value (forecast hours of accepted work), tasks
  and stages done of total, time by phase and its shares, what is in flight, what is ahead with its
  forecast end, the forecast against the date the item or --target keeps, and a burn-up by day
runs.mjs progress --period <date> [--until <date>]
  the delivery metrics the records can name (lead time, change failure rate), and the two they cannot
  (deployment frequency, time to restore), said plainly
runs.mjs gaps      spans that ended with no receipt: recovered here, or named where they are not
runs.mjs time [--since <date>] [--until <date>] [--item <id>] [--no-transcripts]
runs.mjs stalled | pace [--tasks N] | report | list
runs.mjs forecast --scope <issue> --stated "<the date or duration it stands beside>" --set <task ids, comma separated>
  the forecast record a date promised in a document stands beside: the measured pace over exactly the
  tasks covering the outcomes that date serves, and that set's digest. The backlog gate refuses a date
  with no record, a record for another date, and a record whose task set has changed since
Where the project agreed to Jev, --config <gate config> lets it place a session whose working copy is gone and whose
transcript never names the item: only a sure yes counts, and the ones it is unsure of are named on stderr.
The current session is found by itself where the harness names it (Claude Code, Codex, pi); else --harness
claude-code|codex|pi|omp|prime-agent --session <id>.
Transcripts belong to the project by its git repository: [--project <name>] [--repo <path>]. Add --json for data.
Exit 0 done, 2 misuse, 3 the transcript is on another machine. exec exits with the command's own code, 124 when it was stopped past its bound, 127 when it did not start.

title: Order retention-plan pages by the numeric sequence so a traversal across 9/10 skips no plan
description:
Found by the lifemodel-653.8.21 worker (2026-10-25) while checking every list for the end-of-list
defect. `loader/src/storage-retention.ts` (~670) selects `sequence::text` and orders by bare
`sequence`, which binds the text alias and sorts lexically, while `WHERE sequence > $1` compares
the bigint column. With pending plans 9, 10, 11 and limit=1 the traversal starts at 10 and skips 9.
The core's later rescan can revisit it, so a plan is delayed, not lost. The same defect in the
own-space object list was fixed in 653.8.21 (`ORDER BY o.sequence`).

Criterion: a retention-plan traversal with limit=1 over plans whose sequences cross a decimal width
(9/10 or 99/100) returns each plan exactly once in numeric order. Disproved by such a traversal
skipping or repeating a plan.

title: Research a work tracker for a swarm of agents writing from many pods: beads server mode, beads_rust, alternatives, or our own
description:
Owner, 2026-10-13: lifemodel's tasks will run as a swarm of agents (prime-agent per task, Kubernetes Jobs in separate pods, ADR-010), writing to a work tracker often and needing it in sync. Gitea Issues does not fit a swarm (human-oriented API, no atomic claim, no ready queue); beads_rust as used in this repository keeps one SQLite per machine and syncs across machines only through a JSONL file in git (landing PRs, `sync --merge` tombstoning), and pods share no filesystem. The owner reports that beads' server mode gives a lot of merge headaches. The madarch project has the same need, so the answer may be a shared product.

Read with to-research from primary sources (docs, repositories, issue trackers, release notes).

Candidates: beads (Go, steveyegge/beads) including its current storage and server/multi-agent mode — why it causes merge trouble, from its docs and issues; beads_rust (br); file-based trackers (Backlog.md, Taskmaster); trackers with an API built for people (Plane, Gitea Issues); our own thin tracker on Postgres (CloudNativePG, already in ADR-010) with a br-compatible CLI surface and the same JSONL export, so the shady2k-skills adapter, gate and time records keep working.

Criteria: concurrent writes from many pods and machines; atomic claim (compare-and-set); sync without git merges; dependencies and a ready queue; CLI, MCP and change events; self-hosting footprint and licence; fit with the shady2k-skills adapter (beads JSONL export).

Out: building or installing anything; choosing where a shared product lives (owner's decision after the record).

## DONE WHEN
A research record with a recommendation (adopt X / build our own, and where) and its evidence, ready for the outcome-6 and outcome-7 designs and usable by madarch.

title: Research the agent harness inside a task and the S3 store for task artifacts before lifemodel-653 is designed
description:
Owner decisions 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 on lifemodel-653: the harness is replaceable behind one seam, prime-agent one candidate, others (e.g. a DeepSeek agent harness) compared before the design picks the first; task output and artifacts live in S3-compatible storage in the cluster, MinIO out (archived 2026-04-25); candidates RustFS and SeaweedFS (Garage noted).

Harness: per candidate, can it run headless in a Job from one prompt/briefing to a result; take an arbitrary OpenAI-compatible endpoint (the model gateway) from env with no key and no config file; honour HTTPS_PROXY; tool and shell support; how it reports progress and a final result; resume/stop; license, maturity, image size. S3: per candidate, single-node k3s fit (memory at idle and under load on the 11 GB dev machine, Helm chart or manifests, persistence), the S3 operations we need (put/get/list/delete, presigned GET for owner download, per-prefix credentials or policies so a task can write only its own prefix without a long-lived key), license, maturity, backup. Desk research plus small local probes where cheap; no cluster changes.

## DONE WHEN
docs/research/task-runtime.md compares the harness candidates and the S3 candidates against the criteria above, each claim sourced or probed, and ends with one recommendation for each plus what would change it; the owner has read the summary.

comments.author: claude-code-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:main#d388c27e
comments.text: Owner trade 1 answered 2026-10-20 (artifact path). Owner: 'если дать права джобе записывать в хранилище напрямую, то мы убираем привязку к ядру. Может быть ядро должно выделять хранилище для задачи, задача им может пользоваться. А потом ядро решает что делать с этим хранилищем.' then 'сам SeaweedFS нужно закрыть отдельным модулем хранилища. То есть все запросы на хранение идут через новый модуль. Мы абстрагируем всех от реализации.' then 'Да' to: a storage module (a separate in-cluster service, the model gateway's pattern, ADR-013) is the only holder of SeaweedFS credentials; tasks, the core and the web reach storage only through it. The core asks the module to allocate a task's space at launch, seal it at the end (read-only, manifest of marked files with hashes, delete the rest) and apply retention/pins/ceiling/warnings. A task talks to the module directly (not through the core) with its projected ServiceAccount token; the module validates the live task and confines it to its own space itself, so revocation is immediate and the boundary does not rest on SeaweedFS IAM. API: the module's own small API (put, get, list, mark as result), a small CLI in the workbench used by the harness as a tool; S3 stays internal to the module. Owner downloads go through the web interface to the module. Cost accepted: all bytes pass the module.

comments.author: claude-code-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:main#d388c27e
comments.text: Owner trade 2 answered 2026-10-20 (Stop): 'Мягкая остановка - это дать агенту самому завершить работу, это точно не несколько секунд. Ну и жесткий таймаут.' Stop = the harness inside the task is told to wrap up by itself (finish the current step, save and mark what it has, write its result) with no new external effects allowed; a hard deadline then removes the Job whatever its state. The hard deadline is a setting (coordinator's proposed default: 5 minutes). The same soft-then-hard sequence applies when a task reaches the timeout the agent set.

comments.author: claude-code-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:main#d388c27e
comments.text: Owner 2026-10-20 clarifying Stop: 'Может быть дать обе возможности? У нас же была вот эта кнопка паника?' then 'Я к тому, чтобы дать обе возможности и мягкую остановку и жесткую'. Two stops: soft Stop (the harness wraps up, hard deadline from settings, default 5 min) and hard 'stop now' (the Job is removed at once; only what was already marked and stored is kept), from the panel or in words.

title: The loader saves and shows the task concurrency setting from one typed declaration, drawn by a generated control
description:
Prefactor + first slice (ADR-014 D6, T10). Shared pure TypeScript declaration types and validators (key, typed default, label/description locale keys, section, control, data class, bounds/unit, options, authority, apply timing; secrets: no getter, set/delete/exists only), a platform-owned Postgres settings scope with revisions written by the loader through narrow operations, loader HTTP read/write, and generated kit controls in the loader UI — no per-setting switch. First declaration: tasks.concurrency, number 1..8, default 2. Built so the web interface can later host its own declarations with the same library.

tests/unit/task-settings-registry.test.ts: a duplicate key, unknown key, wrong type and out-of-bounds value are refused with the declaration's reason, and normally a valid value is stored with a new revision; a secret declaration exposes no read; in the loader UI the concurrency control renders from the declaration (a test adds a second declaration and it renders with no UI change); the value survives a loader restart.

comments.author: claude-code-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:main#d388c27e
comments.text: Owner 2026-10-20: 'А зачем загрузчику postgre? Он по идее не должен ни от чего зависеть. Можно быть просто в файле json хранить?' — the loader is the platform's root and must not depend on Postgres (it provisions it). Platform settings live in a JSON file on the loader's own volume (/var/lib/loader, beside auth.json and onboarding.json), written atomically with a revision; this replaces the 'platform-owned Postgres settings scope' of ADR-014 D6. Consumers (core, storage module) read a read-only projection the loader publishes (coordinator's proposal: a ConfigMap only the loader can write), so they do not depend on the loader being up and cannot change the values.

comments.author: claude-code-coordinator
comments.text:
Decision log, stage-2 run (coordinator, 2026-10-20; owner agreed to run: "Бери"; owner away now, back later for a couple of hours: decisions only he can make are pushed to his phone at once, independent work continues).
1. The storage module ships in the loader image as its own entry point and service account, like the model gateway (ADR-015 S-D1 "like model gateway"); no new image or signature.
2. 653.7.2 was too large for one worker session; split into 653.7.2 (identity and revoke, S02), 653.7.5 (objects, S03), 653.7.6 (seal, S04), 653.7.7 (pressure, S10). 653.7.3 and 653.7.4 now wait for 653.7.6.
3. The access projection's SQL table is defined in this stage as the storage module's read contract; its writer (the gateway's binding reconciliation, ADR-015 S-D2) comes with stage 3; tests seed it.
4. Workers: deepseek-v4.1-flash-auto; 653.7.2 (identity/revoke) to gpt-6.1-sol as the hardest security work; stage review gpt-6.1-sol, deepseek as a second opinion on the security tasks. One worker at a time (machine memory).
5. Test-VM walks (7.1 deploy, 7.4 restore) by the coordinator through the signed platform artifact; restore is proved within one machine, no disk-loss promise (ADR-015 S-D7).
6. Each task lands as its own pull request, merged by the coordinator once green (owner, 2026-10-20). Digest pushed once a day at the end of the owner's working day.

comments.author: claude-code-coordinator
comments.text:
Open question for the owner (coordinator, 2026-10-21), stage 2 stops here: lifemodel-653.7.2's worker (gpt-6.1-sol) stopped before writing code, rightly. The storage module needs its own Postgres access (ADR-015: SQL rights only on its catalog and the narrow access read), but the motor-1 charter puts per-module store credentials through OpenBao (lifemodel-2t5) out of this milestone, and nothing in the platform gives a module its own database role today: core uses the database owner's login, web runs on core's credentials (owner decision 2026-10-15, until 2t5). Two more gaps follow: the database exists only in platform C while the module sits in A (a readiness cycle), and ADR-015 wants task tokens over TLS, which no internal service has yet.
Recommendation (A): an interim like web's, narrower: the storage module gets its own Postgres login, created by CNPG, with rights only on the storage schema and a read of the access projection, its password kept in a Secret only the module mounts (the same shape as SeaweedFS's identity); lifemodel-2t5 later replaces it with leased credentials. The module moves to a platform step after the database; its task/control listeners get a certificate from the instance CA. Cost: about two more tasks in this stage (half a day of agent time).
Alternatives: (B) take the SQL half of lifemodel-2t5 into motor-1 now (Bank-Vaults webhook, vault-env, leased roles): the target form at once, a feature-sized addition, days. (C) the module on core's credentials, as web: fastest, but the module gets every right core has, which ADR-015 forbids; not recommended.

comments.author: claude-code-coordinator
comments.text:
Owner decision 2026-10-21 (answer to the open question above): "Берем C. Это промежуточный вариант. Его мы никому не показываем, у нас greenfield." The storage module uses core's Postgres credentials (the database owner's login, as core and web do) until lifemodel-2t5 gives it its own identity in target form: its service account -> an OpenBao role -> leased credentials scoped to the storage schema and the access-projection read (ADR-015 S-D1/S-D2). This is an interim, not shown to anyone, greenfield: no compatibility owed when 2t5 replaces it. ADR-015's SQL-scoping requirement stands as the target; the interim is recorded as an amendment there.
Coordinator's follow-ups, decided alone within the ADR: (1) the storage module moves out of platform step A into a platform step after the database (C), so its catalog-aware readiness (S-D7) cannot block A; SeaweedFS and its custody stay in A. (2) The module's task/control/read listeners serve TLS from the instance CA, as ADR-015 requires for bearer tokens. Both go into a new task, lifemodel-653.7.8, which lifemodel-653.7.2 now waits for.

title: The isolated test store runs out of its 512 MiB Postgres volume as integration suites grow, failing late tests at random
description:
Found during lifemodel-653.7.3 (2026-10-22): one full `node scripts/test-isolated.mjs check` run passed
3958 tests and then failed creating a per-worker database: the disposable test Postgres ran out of space
(ENOSPC) on its fixed 512 MiB tmpfs data volume (`scripts/test-isolated.mjs:180`, `size=512m`). Each
storage integration file creates a full-schema database; the storage suites of stage 2 keep adding them.
The worker avoided it by merging test files, which only postpones it. CI's ci-product runs the same
launcher, so the same failure will turn pull requests red at random as the suite grows.

What a person does: runs `npm run check` (or opens a PR). What happens: sometimes a late test fails with
ENOSPC in store setup. What should happen: the store has room for the whole suite with a stated margin,
or per-worker databases are dropped when their file finishes.

Fix direction (pick in the fix, test the policy): drop each per-worker database after its file (helper in
`tests/helpers/test-stores.ts`), or size the tmpfs from a measured peak plus margin, keeping the test
container's own caps; the entrypoint policy tests pin whatever is chosen.

## DONE WHEN
The full check runs five times in a row without ENOSPC, and a test proves the store's peak usage over the
whole suite stays under 70% of its volume; it is falsified by any ENOSPC in store setup.

title: The web chat's watcher-connection test counts other test files' Valkey clients, so a full check fails at random
description:
Found during lifemodel-653.7.4 (2026-10-22): one full `node scripts/test-isolated.mjs check` failed in
`tests/integration/web-owner-message.test.ts:413` "closes the watcher Valkey connection when the HTTP client
disconnects" (observed client ids ['24','25'] where one was expected). The test treats every new client in
`CLIENT LIST` as the SSE watcher's own connection, but `CLIENT LIST` is server-wide: a client that a test file in
the other vitest worker opens (on another logical database) between the baseline read and the poll is counted
too. Reproduced on an untouched detached origin/main (75729b60): 3 of 3 runs fail with a concurrent file that
opens Valkey connections; the file alone passes 6 of 6 on main and on the branch. CI's ci-product runs the same
launcher, so pull requests can turn red at random.

What a person does: runs `npm run check` (or opens a PR). What happens: rarely, this test fails although the
watcher closed its connection. What should happen: the test counts only its own connections.

Fix direction: filter `CLIENT LIST` by the file's own logical database (db=8) and/or name the watcher's client
(`CLIENT SETNAME`) and filter on the name; never weaken the "closed after disconnect" assertion.

DONE WHEN: the test passes 5 of 5 runs alongside a concurrent file that keeps opening Valkey connections
(the reproduction that fails 3 of 3 today), and still fails when the watcher's connection is left open.

title: The stage-2 acceptance review's defects are fixed: same-space core reads never delay seal, control SQL is independent of reads, and the module checks the persisted owner notice
description:
Stage-2 acceptance review (gpt-6.1-sol, 2026-10-23, at main 8b5f8043) found defects against the agreed stage; they are fixed here before the stage is accepted (not new scope, not a budgeted finding).

1. M1: a same-space core read of a retained marked object delays seal: seal waits for every S3 operation keyed by the space, and core GETs are tracked under that key, so seal answers 503 cleanup_pending after 5 s while such a read is in flight (reproduced: storage-module-seal foreign-space core-read test switched to the same space returns 503). docs/features/motor/storage-seal.md says core reads never enter that barrier.
2. M2: the two reserved control workers share the four-client seal SQL pool with core read guards; four reads waiting on row locks of other spaces delay an unrelated /allocate by 5 s (reproduced: 5012 ms against < 2 s).
3. M3: the module accepts warningCommitted with any well-formed messageId from authenticated core; ADR-015 S-D5 requires the matching persisted owner-notice receipt. Coordinator decision: keep the ADR guarantee: core exposes a narrow read contract of its persisted owner notices and the module checks the receipt exists before it starts the deletion clock (same pattern as the task_access projection read contract).
4. D1/D2: ADR-015 and docs/features/motor/storage-*.md describe built code as future work and name a nonexistent setting (preDeletionWarningLeadSeconds); restore-health fields and the Seaweed rollout strategy differ from the code.

DONE WHEN: a permanent same-space core-read + seal regression passes; control calls ACK < 2 s while core reads hold every read SQL client (the review's probe made permanent); warningCommitted with a messageId that has no persisted owner notice is refused (real core store + real module test) and the shipped core path still confirms; the docs and ADR describe main; full check exit 0.

title: The storage module proves each task's identity on every call and revokes a task's access at once: TokenReview, live Pod/Job binding and the access projection, checked per chunk
description:
ADR-015 S-D2 (identity, independent authorization, immediate revocation); check S02. Split from the original 653.7.2 at the stage-2 run (coordinator, 2026-10-20): objects (S03), seal (S04) and pressure (S10) are 653.7.5-.7.

The module's task listener authenticates a freshly read projected lifemodel-task-storage token by audience-specific TokenReview, then verifies the bound Pod UID, its live non-deleting Pod and controller Job by current API reads (never a watch cache), and the space binding, read together with the committed lifecycle access intent in one narrow SQL read (S-D2): a newer stop/revoke intent wins even before the projection catches up; effective mode from absolute softDueAt/hardStopAt by the database clock. Missing projection or binding fails closed. Core and web use their own audiences on their own listeners; web cannot call control. revoke(space, expectedRevision, effectKey) is keyed, increments the space's access revision, cancels active streams and is linearizable at its ACK. The projection's table is defined here as the storage module's read contract; its writer (the gateway's binding reconciliation) comes with stage 3, so tests seed it. No real Jobs yet: test identities in the isolated suite.

## DONE WHEN
tests/integration/storage-module-auth.test.ts with two task spaces passes: wrong audience, token, Pod UID, deleted Pod or Job, missing projection and an older projection after a committed revoke intent are each refused; core down does not stop a task's own access; a revoke during a PUT and a GET lets no chunk authorize after the revoke ACK; soft wrap allows own-space data only; hard deadline by the database clock denies task operations without any worker having run.

(fresh projected token per call, TLS verified against the instance CA only), writes one ordinary batched
owner notice per plan through its existing durable outbound path keyed by the plan ID (no LLM involved), and
only after that outbound event is committed calls warningCommitted(planId, messageId). Replays and restarts
never send a second notice; core or chat down means the module deletes nothing.

## DONE WHEN
An integration test against a fake module control server and real stores: a pending plan yields exactly one
outbound notice and one warningCommitted with that message's ID; a restart between the outbound commit and
warningCommitted sends no second notice and completes the call; two plans yield two notices; a module
refusal or outage leaves the plan pending and is retried; it is falsified if any path calls warningCommitted
before the outbound commit.

title: The core's error-disposition outbox test fails at random in the full check and can turn any pull request red
description:
Found during lifemodel-653.7.7 (2026-10-23): PR #116's first `ci-product` run (Actions run 39886110928, attempt 1) failed 1 of 4348 tests in `tests/integration/turn-ownership-outbox.test.ts` "leaves error-disposition inbound work unsettled for restart retry" (test at line 447) with `AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`. The branch touched no `src/` core file; the same test passed in four local full checks of that branch and on the rerun. CI's ci-product runs the same isolated launcher, so any pull request can turn red at random, as lifemodel-653.7.11 did.

What a person does: opens a PR or runs `npm run check`. What happens: rarely, this core test fails although the code under it did not change. What should happen: the test waits for the event it checks and is independent of the other Vitest worker's load.

Suspects to check first: the test drives a 10 ms tick and polls `store.read()` from inside a synchronous `waitFor` predicate (`void store.read().then(...)`), so its observation lags the predicate by one read; any later assertion on a list read right after a commit may run before that commit's outbox/snapshot is visible under CPU load. AGENTS.md: "an assertion waits for the event it checks, never for a tick count or a timer".

DONE WHEN: the failure is reproduced under load (the test file alongside a CPU- or Valkey-heavy concurrent file, several runs), the cause is named, the test waits for the actual committed event, and it passes 5 of 5 runs under the same load while still failing when the error-disposition path settles the input (plant that mutation).

title: Two simultaneous PUTs of one upload to the storage module can answer 409 instead of replaying the one receipt
description:
Seen 2026-10-23 on PR #118's ci-product (Actions run 39921758199, attempt 1), a test-only change in another file: `tests/integration/storage-module-objects.test.ts` "serializes simultaneous same-upload reservations and returns one receipt" (line 544) got statuses `[200, 409]` instead of `[200, 200]`. Two identical PUTs of the same upload ID at once must serialize and both return the one receipt (docs/features/motor/storage-objects.md: the same upload ID re-reserves its unchanged metadata; a completed-ID retry replays its saved receipt). Not a finding: a required check caught it on the way to a merge (to-backlog lane rule); it can turn any PR or main red, and if the module really answers 409 (`upload_conflict` or `upload_expired` in loader/src/storage-objects.ts:356/375) to a concurrent duplicate, a task CLI retry after a lost reply gets a false conflict.

What a person does: a task's storage CLI retries a PUT whose first reply was lost while the first is still being published, or the full check runs under load. What happens: rarely, 409. What should happen: the duplicate waits for the first and replays its receipt (200, same JSON), one object, charged once.

## DONE WHEN
Reproduced under load (the file beside a CPU-heavy concurrent file, several runs; or by a fault point that delays the first PUT between reservation and publication); the cause named (module race vs test); if the module: the duplicate serializes on the upload intent and replays the receipt, with a deterministic test using the delay point; 5 of 5 under load; mutation (drop the serialization) goes red.

title: The platform runs its own zot registry, imports the pinned workbench into it at first start, and task Jobs pull their image only from it
description:
Owner decision 2026-10-24 (stage 3 VM walk): "Ну это же глупость. Подними zot сейчас" / "Да, давай" — the task workbench is served from the instance's own zot registry now, not pulled from ghcr.io; pwe's in-cluster builds later push to the same zot. Plain HTTP on a stable node-resolvable endpoint, push by password from OpenBao, anonymous pull from the node (owner 2026-10-19 on pwe: "zot по паролю, но потом TLS"; TLS stays lifemodel-pwe.2). The bootstrap set (k3s, Flux, zot itself, loader) stays release-pinned by digest and is not served from zot: nothing could fill zot before the loader runs.

Criterion: on a fresh install the platform runs zot with one persistent volume; the loader's first start imports the release-pinned workbench into zot byte-identical (same manifest digest, verified); the node's registries.yaml (NixOS module and generic installer) names the zot endpoint; core's workbench launch input, the core executor and the CEL Job-shape guards accept only the zot repository by digest; a task Job pulls the workbench from zot with ghcr.io unreachable; an anonymous push and a push by any pod but the loader are refused; ADR-010 decision 4 is amended (zot replaces registry:2, interim plain HTTP). Disproved by: a Job image from ghcr.io or any other repository admitted, a digest changed by the import, or a push accepted without the password.

Left out: TLS for the registry (lifemodel-pwe.2); serving core, web, loader or gateway from zot (pwe, with the in-cluster build); air-gapped install.

title: The loader's settings name the registry the workbench is imported from, the import runs as a retriable loader task outside first start, and no source registry is hard-coded
description:
Owner decisions 2026-10-24:
- "Ну получается нужно собрать его через CI. И публиковать новый, если что-то изменилось."
- "А зачем мы хардкодим ghcr.io? А если пользователь захочет использовать свой registry? Вынеси это в загрузчик."

Today (653.8.13) the loader's first-start phase imports the workbench only from ghcr.io/shady2k/lifemodel-workbench. The host is hard-coded in the importer, the seed-pin check and the docs, and the import blocks first start.

The change: the workbench source registry/repository becomes a loader setting.
- It is set in the loader's settings like the model endpoint, defaults to the project's published origin, and may carry an optional pull credential kept in OpenBao.
- The digest stays release-pinned, and integrity is the digest check, not trust in a host.
- The importer confines its requests to the configured registry host. On a redirect it never forwards credentials and verifies every byte by digest.
- The import is a retriable loader task outside the blocking first-start chain: the platform comes up while the source is unreachable or not yet set. Changing the setting re-runs the import. Core refuses a task launch with a clear reason until the pinned workbench is in zot. The loader's interface shows the import state and its safe reason.

Criterion:
- On a fresh install the platform comes up with the source unreachable.
- Setting the source to another registry (the owner's https://registry.inside.shady2k.ru) imports the pinned digest byte-identical into zot.
- A task then runs from zot.
- A wrong digest at the source is refused.
- A credential never appears in logs, the settings dump or errors.
- No ghcr.io literal remains outside the default value and docs.

Disproved by: first start blocked on the source, the import following an off-host target with credentials, or a task Job admitted before the workbench is in zot.

Left out: serving core/web/loader from zot (pwe); TLS to zot (pwe.2).

title: Roll zot when its configuration changes
description:
Found in the stage-3 VM walk (2026-10-25): after a platform upgrade changed `deploy/platform/a/zot.yaml` (added `http.compat`), Flux applied the new `zot-config` ConfigMap but `zot-0` kept running with the old config (pod created before the change, 0 restarts, `/etc/zot/config.json` in the pod without the new key). title: Retry the task launcher's channel connection while the pod's network policy is still being applied
description:
Found in the stage-3 VM walk (2026-10-25), twice: every task fails at once with `request_unavailable` then `terminal_unavailable`; no briefing, no result, no file.

Evidence (capture on the node, second run): the task pod resolves core.lifemodel.svc -> 10.42.0.32 and sends one SYN to :8447 ~7 ms after DNS; it never reaches core's veth; no SYN retransmit. kube-router (k3s embedded network policy) answers denied traffic with `REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable`. `task-channel-ingress` (core ingress from lifemodel-motor task pods) has no iptables rule while no task pod exists; it gains the new pod IP only after kube-router syncs. Measured on this node: a new pod is cut off for 0.2–0.5 s after start (3 probes: 212/419/525 ms). The launcher's first call (`/task/identity`) lands inside that window, fails in milliseconds with a connection error, and is never retried; the terminal report follows inside the same window. Core logs nothing (the request never reaches it).

Criterion: a task whose pod starts inside the network-policy propagation window still reads identity and briefing and reports its terminal. Connection-level failures that happen before any request byte is sent (ECONNREFUSED, EHOSTUNREACH, ENETUNREACH, ICMP-unreachable, connect timeout) are retried with bounded backoff inside a startup window (the phase deadline, not unbounded). `/task/start` keeps its exactly-once rule: it is never resent once any byte may have left; a pure connect failure before sending may be retried only if that is provably safe, otherwise left as is with the reason stated.

Disproved by: a test where the first N connects are refused and the launcher still fails; a retry after request bytes were sent on `/task/start`; unbounded retries.

Out: changing kube-router or the network policies; a readiness gate on the pod (could be a later improvement).

title: Make the model gateway send the slot's configured model for task requests instead of the harness's model name
description:
Found in the stage-3 VM walk from a clean snapshot (2026-10-25, revision 3463f721). The task pod
started, reached the task relay and the model gateway, but every model request of the task failed
with `upstream_503` (gateway log, 08:53:25–08:54:56 UTC); core's own model calls through the same
primary slot succeeded before and after (08:52:51, 08:55:23). The task ended without the script or
fib.txt; the owner saw "a restriction on creating the file".

Cause (code): the workbench harness configures OpenCode with the model `lifemodel/task`
(`loader/src/task-opencode.ts`), so the task sends `"model": "task"`. The gateway replaces the
model with the slot's configured model only for the reserve slot or for `"model": "default"`
(`loader/src/model-gateway-app.ts`, the body built before the upstream request); for the primary
slot it forwards `"task"`, which the owner's endpoint does not serve (it answers 503). Core sends
`default` (`DEFAULT_ROLE_MODEL`), which is why its calls pass. Every gateway test uses
`model: 'default'`, so this path was never exercised.

Criterion: a task's model request through the task relay reaches the upstream with the slot's
configured model, whatever model name the harness puts in the request; the harness cannot choose
the upstream model. Disproved by: a task-traffic request (trusted task id) with `model: "task"` or
any other name arriving upstream with a model other than the slot's configured one; or a test suite
where no task-path request uses a model name other than `default`.

Direction: for trusted task traffic the gateway owns the model (as it already owns the task's
identity fields), on both slots; keep core's `default` behaviour. Add unit/integration tests for the
task path with a non-default model name, and check the harness config still matches (one name, no
vendor leak).

title: Make the task launcher stop listing stored objects at the storage module's real end of list
description:
Found in the stage-3 VM walk (2026-10-25, loader at 0586f194, after the 653.8.20 fix). The model
answered the task (no gateway failures), but the task ended `failed` with
`reasonCode: "artifact_limit"`, an empty `result.txt` and a 650-byte log; the owner got no fib.txt.

Cause (code): the storage module's own-space list (`loader/src/storage-objects.ts`) always answers
`nextCursor: cursor(space, page.at(-1)?.sequence ?? after)` — a string, also on an empty last page
(docs/features/motor/storage-objects.md: "Continue from the returned opaque cursor"; no end marker is
documented). The storage CLI passes it through (`loader/src/storage-cli.ts` accepts null or a
string). The task launcher's `artifacts()` (`loader/src/task-launcher.ts`) stops only on
`nextCursor === null`, so it pages through empty pages until its 100-page cap and throws
`artifact_limit` — for every task, with or without artifacts. Each side's tests used a fake that
follows its own reading of the contract.

Criterion: a task that marks 0, 1 or 64 artifacts reports its terminal with exactly those artifact
ids; a task with 65 still fails `artifact_limit`. Disproved by a launcher run against the real
storage module list (or a fake that answers exactly as the module does, including the empty last
page with a cursor) that ends `artifact_limit` with fewer than 65 artifacts.

Direction: settle the list contract once (an explicit end: `nextCursor: null` on the last page, or

title: A task whose agent recovered from a failed command is reported as failed
description:
## What happens
Owner asks for long work in chat; the task Job runs (walk 2026-10-25 14:46Z, launch 7c1d7594…), the agent uses tools 8 times and ends its turn, and the outcome is `failed` / `required_tool_failed` with an empty result.txt. No output files are delivered.

## Cause (code)
`loader/src/task-acp.ts` `result()` fails the task when ANY tool call ever had status `failed` or `toolOutputFailed()` was true (`this.toolFailed` is sticky). `loader/src/task-opencode.ts` `toolOutputFailed` marks every shell command with a non-zero `exit` as failed. So a probing or intermediate command (`which python`, a failing test before its fix, `ls missing`) fails the whole task even when the agent recovered and finished.

## Requirement it breaks
docs/features/motor/task-harness.md and ADR-014: success requires end_turn, final text and no provider error or **unresolved** required tool failure. A failure the agent later recovered from is not unresolved; a non-zero exit of an ordinary command is not a required-tool failure.

## Should happen
- A tool call that failed and is followed by further agent work and a final `end_turn` answer does not fail the task.
- Still failed: provider error; a tool call still pending/in_progress at end; no end_turn or empty final text; a failure after which the agent did nothing more (the last settled tool failed and the turn ended with no final text) — exact rule decided by the worker against the spec, stated in task-harness.md.
- The background-command fail-closed rule is reviewed under the same principle (unobserved result ≠ task failure if the agent continued).

## Diagnosis
Moved to lifemodel-653.8.24 (run trace in the database); this task builds on it and verifies the fix on the VM with `lifemodel doctor trace last`.

## Checks
Unit tests in tests/unit for task-acp result classification: recovered failure → succeeded; trailing failure / unsettled tool → failed. Full isolated check.
Disproved if a task whose agent ran a failing command and then finished is still reported failed.

title: A task run is recorded as a trace in the database and shows which tool call failed
description:
## Why
A failed task run cannot be explained today. The 2026-10-25 14:46Z walk ended `failed / required_tool_failed`; the retained `log.jsonl` holds only fixed lines ("Task is using a tool" x8), no tool, status, exit code or agent text, and the pod's stdout is gone with the Job. ADR-014 already allows the retained task log to be private content ("Retained task logs are private content in storage, not process diagnostic logging; strip credential material"); the launcher applied process-diagnostic redaction to it instead.

## Owner decision (2026-10-25)
Run traces live in the database, not in a file, modelled on hermes-lifemodel's observability store (github.com/shady2k/hermes-lifemodel: `state/trace_store.py`, `log.py`, `core/turn_recorder.py`, `activity.py`):
- a SEPARATE, DISPOSABLE store: Postgres schema `observability` (own migration in db/migrations), tables `trace_spans` (trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, component, started_at, ended_at, status, attrs jsonb) and `trace_events` (record id, trace_id, span_id, event, ts, fields jsonb); generic, so core ticks can use it later;
- fail-OPEN: writes are asynchronous from a bounded queue, batched; a full queue or failed write drops the record and bumps a counter; a trace write never blocks or fails a tick, a task or its outcome. The state schemas stay fail-closed;
- closed span status set {ok, failed, suppressed}; an unknown host status maps to failed, never ok; an open span reads as incomplete;
- retention by age (default 14 days) / count / size, whole traces only, never an open trace.

## What to build
1. Task run = one trace, child of the core turn that called `core.startTask` (carry its trace id). Root span: task id, launch id, harness, outcome, reasonCode. Children: model calls (duration, stop reason, token usage where ACP gives it), tool calls (kind, title/command, status, exit code, duration, bounded output tail), agent final text (bounded). A failed outcome's root names the span that caused it.
2. The launcher sends these as structured trace frames over the existing task channel to core (:8447); the pod gets no DB access. Trace frames are fail-open and bounded (size per field, count per run); they must not ride the durable step/terminal mailbox semantics if that makes a trace loss block the run — decide and document in task-channel.md.
3. Credential stripping on everything that lands in the store (no secrets are in the pod by design; still scrub token-like values and the known token file paths' contents).
4. Drop the fixed-line `log.jsonl` as the run journal (and its storage upload) unless kept as an export of the trace; record the choice in task-harness.md and storage-objects.md.
5. Loader, core and gateway diagnostic lines about a task carry task id and trace id (fixed codes stay; no content there).
6. Reader: `lifemodel doctor trace <trace_id | last [N]>` renders the span tree (deploy/cli), like hermes `activity turn <id>`.

## Left out
Moving core tick tracing onto this store (deferred task); a web UI view.

## Checks
Unit/integration tests: span tree persisted for a fake harness run with a failed tool; full queue drops and counts without failing the run; unknown status → failed; retention never prunes an open trace; credential canaries absent from the store. Full isolated check. Disproved if a failed run on the VM does not show, via `lifemodel doctor trace last`, which tool call failed and its exit code.

title: Task trace scrubbing redacts the whole Authorization header value for every scheme, not only Bearer and Basic
description:
Found in the round-2 coordinator check of PR #140 (lifemodel-653.8.24, merged 784f3b63).

The trace scrubbers (`loader/src/task-trace-channel.ts`, `src/storage/postgres-trace-store.ts`) redact `Authorization: Bearer <credential>` and `Authorization: Basic <credential>` whole. For any other scheme (`Authorization: Token <opaque>`, `Digest …`, `ApiKey …`, custom schemes) the single-word assignment pass consumes only the scheme word, so an opaque credential with no recognisable token shape stays in `command`/`outputTail`, is stored in `observability.trace_spans` and is shown by `lifemodel doctor trace`.

What a person does: a task runs `curl -v -H 'Authorization: Token opaque123' …`. What happens: the stored span reads `Authorization: [REDACTED] opaque123`. What should happen: the whole header value after `Authorization:` is redacted, whatever the scheme. Requirement: ADR-014 — retained task records hold no credentials.

Done when: both scrubbers redact the complete Authorization value for any scheme (scheme plus credential, up to the end of the header value), with canaries through the real transport and real DB rows for `Token`, `Digest` and an unknown scheme; existing Bearer/Basic/quoted canaries stay green.

title: The trace container stop test bounds the coordinator deadline by clock reads on both sides of the stop call

title: Task trace frames are accepted during a normal run, so a finished run's trace has no open tool spans
description:
Found in the stage-3 VM walk (2026-10-25 22:47Z, main 7e2b261f: core f0592eed, loader 2f5d819a, workbench f6f92520). Task task_e961aa25… succeeded (state done; the recovered `ls` failure did not fail it — lifemodel-653.8.23 holds), but its trace is incomplete.

The terminal report and outcome were accepted, so these were very likely `POST /task/trace` frames. The second tool span (`shell`, started 22:48:22.487) stayed open (`ended_at` null, `[incomplete]` in `lifemodel doctor trace last`), so the trace shows a tool still running in a run that succeeded. 5 spans stored, 0 events.

Should happen: on an idle single-task VM, trace frames are accepted; the trace of a completed run has every tool span closed. A refusal line names the route and, after authentication, the task and trace ids (fixed codes, no content).

Likely area: the trace authority path in `src/core/task-channel.ts` / `src/storage/postgres-task-mailbox.ts` `readTraceAuthority` (separate one-connection pool, 250 ms bound) or the observation writer pool, under real Postgres latency. Find the actual cause first (reproduce with the real pool bounds against a real Postgres with ordinary latency).
