title: Probe goose over ACP in the offline workbench and decide whether an ACP harness adapter with goose becomes stage 4's second harness
description:
Serves: lifemodel-653.9 (stage 4: the second harness switched by a setting). Design: ADR-014 D1-D2, checks T02, T07.

Owner raised 2026-10-24: goose (Apache 2.0, Rust, Agentic AI Foundation / Linux Foundation; https://goose-docs.ai/) and its GDK. GDK offers in-process Rust crates (goose-agent, goose-providers, goose-context-management) or ACP (Agent Client Protocol): `goose acp` over stdio, or `goose serve` over HTTP/WebSocket with a secret key. Our launcher is TypeScript, so the fit is ACP over stdio. If the launcher's harness adapter speaks ACP, one adapter serves goose and any other ACP agent, which matches ADR-014's replaceable harness better than one bespoke adapter per agent (OpenCode HTTP/SSE, prime-agent RPC). Stage 3 stays on OpenCode; this decides stage 4's second harness before it is built.

## Probe (in the workbench image, network none except the model gateway relay)
1. A pinned goose binary (version + SHA-256) in the workbench; `goose acp` starts with zero outbound connections other than the relay (session naming off, no allowlist fetch, no telemetry, no keyring) — proven by a network-none run and a connection log.
2. Model calls reach only the gateway through the existing loopback relay (custom OpenAI-compatible provider, base URL = relay).
3. Over ACP: a prompt runs a shell tool; a cancel mid-tool stops it; session/update events stream; a permission request is answered by the launcher; the end yields an unambiguous semantic success or failure.
4. Read the ACP reference: which methods goose implements, version and stability; whether OpenCode also speaks ACP (`opencode acp`) and how completely.

## DONE WHEN
A written result in docs/research (or the ADR-014 decision log) with the evidence of 1-4 and a recommendation: ACP adapter + goose as stage 4's second harness (instead of or beside prime-agent), or not, with why. An accepted yes becomes an ADR-014 amendment before stage 4's tasks are cut. Disproved by: any startup network call that cannot be disabled, no reliable cancel, or no unambiguous final result.

## Left out
Building the ACP adapter or switching stage 3's OpenCode adapter; the GDK Rust SDK (would need a Rust launcher).

title: Idea: the installer lets the owner choose DHCP or a static address for the machine
description:
Owner, 2026-10-21 («Да, на потом»): the installation should let the owner choose how the machine gets its address — DHCP or a static address (address/prefix, gateway, DNS servers) — at install time.

Today: neither `scripts/install.sh` nor the `services.lifemodel` NixOS module (`deploy/nixos/`) sets the host's network; the host's own configuration decides, and the installer only hands the host's usable nameservers to k3s (`deploy/nixos/README.md`, `/run/lifemodel/k3s-resolv.conf`). Matters for real hardware: a static address keeps `<name>.local`, the registry and the owner's bookmarks stable across reboots and router changes.

Questions to settle when picked up: where the choice is made (installer prompt, NixOS option, both); what changing it after install means for k3s's node address and the certificates that name it; whether `.local` mDNS stays the primary name.

Not in motor-1. Review: 2026-11-21.

title: The loader watches the cluster and tells the owner which part is unhealthy and why
description:
Owner, 2026-10-21: «Загрузчик должен следить за статусом кластера.»

Why (the incident it answers): on the test VM the 653.7.5 install stood 26 minutes with platform step D
not Ready — the storage module Pod stuck in ContainerCreating because the node's pod address pool
(10.42.0.0/24, host-local IPAM) was exhausted: 255 leases, 25 live Pods. Nothing reported it; it was
found only by an agent reading Flux conditions and Pod events with kubectl. (The leak itself came from
the walk's own wipe script, not the product; the gap is that the platform said nothing.)

Today: `lifemodel doctor` (lifemodel-lut.4, ryr.4.3) reports Flux sources, Kustomizations, the loader,
OpenBao seal and Gitea — on demand, from a shell. The loader shows first-start phases only. Nothing
watches the running cluster continuously or tells the owner.

Direction (to be chartered with observability-1, beside lifemodel-vbog's logs): the loader watches the
cluster continuously — Flux Kustomizations and sources not Ready, Pods not starting or restarting,
failed Jobs, node pressure and exhausted resources (disk, memory, pod addresses) — shows the state
with a plain reason on its own page (it works when the core or chat is broken), and pushes a
notification to the owner when a part stays unhealthy past a bound. Read-only RBAC; reasons are kinds
and object names, never Secret values.

Feature title only until the milestone is chartered.

## DONE WHEN
On the test VM, with a planted failure (a Pod that cannot start, a Kustomization that stays not Ready),
the loader's page names the failing part and the reason within a minute and the owner gets one
notification; it is falsified if finding the failure needs kubectl.

title: The install guide and doctor state the platform's measured minimum memory, so a 4 GiB machine is warned instead of k3s restarting under load
description:
Found in the from-snapshot walk of lifemodel-avy (2026-10-15) on the test VM (2 vCPU, 3.9 GiB RAM, no swap): with the whole platform up (k3s, Flux, OpenBao, Gitea, CNPG, Valkey, loader, core) free memory fell to ~110 MiB, the page cache thrashed (100-230 MB/s reads, IO pressure full ~20%), k3s's embedded etcd answered in ~1 s, the controllers lost leader election and k3s exited (status 1) at 06:57:28; systemd restarted it 1.5 min later. With 7.9 GiB the same walks ran clean (load ~1).

What a person does: installs lifemodel on a 4 GiB machine as the setup guide allows. What happens: the cluster restarts itself under ordinary load. What should happen: the install guide and `lifemodel doctor` state a measured minimum memory (and the installer or doctor warns below it), the way the x86-64-v2 CPU requirement is stated.

Criterion: deploy/nixos's setup guide names a minimum RAM measured from a full platform's peak (containers-design-review Q11 notes no measured margin exists), and doctor warns below it; and on a machine at or above it, a full bring-up plus the restart walks shows no k3s restart.
Out of scope: reducing the platform's footprint.

title: A small supervisor outside the cluster watches the machine and the cluster and repairs what it safely can, on any Linux host
description:
Owner, 2026-10-21: «Да, давай так и сделаем, маленький supervisor, который следит за кластером и машиной.
Только на nixos не нужно завязываться, это у меня он стоит на nixos.»

Why: everything that repairs the instance today — the loader, `lifemodel doctor`, Flux — runs in or
through k3s. When k3s itself does not start, they are all blind: doctor only reports that kubectl failed.
State of practice: a rescue layer that does not depend on what it rescues (Talos machined/apid outside
Kubernetes, Home Assistant OS below its Supervisor, Rancher's system agent).

Direction (to be chartered with observability-1):
- A small supervisor process on the machine, outside the cluster, depending on nothing it watches
  (not k3s, not Postgres, not OpenBao, not the loader).
- **Not tied to NixOS** (owner): it runs on any supported Linux host and is installed by the generic
  installer (`scripts/install.sh`); the NixOS module is only one way of installing it, not a requirement.
  Host-specific repair (e.g. rolling back a NixOS generation) is an optional adapter, never assumed.
- Watches the machine (k3s service state and its last errors, node readiness, disk, memory) and the
  cluster from outside (API reachable, platform Kustomizations Ready).
- Repairs what it safely can, as named owner-visible actions: restart k3s, re-pin the previous platform
  release (what `lifemodel doctor --repin previous` does today), and later restore from a backup.
- First surface: the CLI over SSH (grow `lifemodel doctor` into it — no new entry point into the
  machine). A LAN rescue page with its own credentials only by a later owner decision (a new attack surface).
- Overlap with lifemodel-7514 (the loader watches the cluster from inside): settle at charter which
  watches what and where the owner reads it; one notification path, never two.

Feature title only until the milestone is chartered.

## DONE WHEN
On a test machine with k3s stopped (and separately with the disk nearly full), the owner runs one command
over SSH and reads which part is broken and why, and one named repair action brings the instance back;
it is falsified if any step needs kubectl, journalctl or knowledge of the host's distribution.

comments.text:
Owner decisions for this feature, 2026-10-14 (planning conversation; asked one at a time):

1. Existing data: there is no live instance. Nothing is imported from data/state or LanceDB; no importer is filed.
2. The docker-run path (outcome 4's single image) is removed in this feature, with no compatibility layer (design principle 5). Until outcome 5 is done, lifemodel runs only as the k3s platform (or locally for development); outcome 4's check is re-walked on k3s by the charter anyway.
3. Telegram leaves the core in this feature and its channel code is deleted; it is not rebuilt as a gateway now - the web chat (lifemodel-vhd) comes first. In this feature messages arrive only through the Valkey `inbound` stream (the design's contract; the walk writes them as a gateway would), and answers go out as events on the outbound stream plus the message row in Postgres. Telegram as a gateway over the inbound stream is a deferred task after the web chat.
4. Tests of the core run against real Valkey and Postgres: the isolated launcher starts them as service containers from the production images (Valkey; the CloudNativePG Postgres image with pgvector), digest-pinned, on an internal network with no egress, removed with the run. The test container still gets no Docker socket. Owner preferred real containers over PGlite/in-container binaries ("контейнеры в docker надежнее"); testcontainers was rejected because it needs the Docker socket inside the test.

Also confirmed: LanceDB is removed; memory and vector search move to pgvector (ADR-010 supersedes ADR-005's storage leg; the local ONNX embedder stays).

Coordinator choices from ADR-010, not objected to:
- store credentials are static Kubernetes Secrets (CNPG-generated, platform-generated for Valkey) until lifemodel-2t5 moves them to OpenBao;
- the core takes the epoch itself at start (Lua CAS) until the generation operator takes it over in lifemodel-pwe;
- Valkey, the CNPG operator and the Postgres cluster are platform-owned (namespace lifemodel-state), unreachable to generations; the core runs as a one-replica StatefulSet in `lifemodel` from the deploy branch.

title: Every core Postgres write checks the active holder, and a stale writer's write is refused
description:
ADR-010 "Fencing" (Q2) and Q4 amendment 5: the snapshot write is epoch-checked in Valkey, and "Postgres `active_holder` keeps the same meaning for keyed pg.apply writes (the core module's apply path checks it)" — a cheap guard against operator bugs (A2: on one node stop-first is the real fence). The stage-2 stores (conversations, memory/graph, soul, recipient registry, kv for plugin settings/schedules/Motor state) write to Postgres directly with no holder check; only the outbox message rows (avy.4.2) are applied after the tick commit. Found during integration of avy.3.4.

Scope: a `core.active_holder` row (the epoch the core took in Valkey at start, written at start with `UPDATE ... SET epoch = $new WHERE epoch < $new`); every core Postgres write transaction checks it (one shared write helper/pool wrapper the stores use) and is refused with a named error when the stored holder is newer than the writer's epoch, and the core stops on such a refusal like on a stale snapshot commit. Out of scope (recorded for the owner): moving every Postgres write to keyed commands applied after the tick commit.

## DONE WHEN
A suite test: core A takes epoch N and writes; core B takes N+1; A's next write through any store (conversation, memory, soul, registry, kv) is refused, nothing of it is visible, and A stops; B's writes succeed. Full isolated check passes.

title: A running core retries a failed internal turn itself, so the bounded ledger never waits for a restart
description:

A running core retries a failed internal turn itself within the same bounded retry policy as inbound (retry once, then the input completes with its recorded failure and a warn), without a restart; a test drives a failed internal head, 100+ later internal signals and shows them all processed in FIFO order by the same core; the reviewer's probes from its report are committed as permanent tests; AGENTS.md states the policy; full isolated check passes.

PASS WITH COMMENTS

# F8 confirmation — lifemodel-avy

Reviewed main `955d403f4d4d6d8a21c3b667218b6da7f4fb58ac` on `review/avy-f8`, including `git show -m 864d2e6 --first-parent`, `.review-f7.md`, the exported lifemodel-avy.6 DONE WHEN clauses, ADR-010's bounded-stop value and AGENTS.md's guarantees. This confirmation covers F8, not a new VM acceptance walk.

## Original F8: CLOSED

Both original failure modes now pass against the actual entrypoint and actual stores inside the disposable test boundary.

Temporary independent probes used `tests/integration/review-f8-exit.test.ts` and `tests/fixtures/review-f8-child.ts`. They applied the real migrations, installed a PostgreSQL BEFORE INSERT trigger on `core.conversation_messages` that raises `review persistent history-store failure` for recipient `review-f8`, and started the real `src/index.ts` through tsx with production mode, Motor disabled, a private test-store database/logical Valkey database and `LIFEMODEL_CORE_STOP_DEADLINE_MS=100`. Each child first reached HTTP health 200 with a committed snapshot; the test then appended a real inbound message. No fatal callback or stop coordinator was reimplemented in these probes.

1. **Clean fatal stop with open listeners — CLOSED.** The rejected insert reached the production fatal callback. The child completed shutdown and exited **1**, without an external signal or a hard-deadline error. The observed fatal-log-to-process-exit interval was 37 ms. It no longer remains alive after `Shutdown complete`.
2. **Stalled registry flush — CLOSED.** The child patched only `PersistentRecipientRegistry.prototype.flush` to record entry and return a never-resolving promise. The same actual rejected insert reached the production fatal callback. The child exited **1** without test timeout/forced cleanup. The hard-exit error named `state_flush`; `Shutdown complete` was absent. The observed fatal-log-to-process-exit interval was 131 ms. This is an external log-observation interval, not an exact timer-fire measurement.

In all three actual-entrypoint cases below, the database cause was present, one shutdown sequence ran, and the durable snapshot observed after normalization failed remained byte-identical through process exit. The retained `user-history-restart.test.ts` also passed: failed normalization makes health 503, commits no failed snapshot even during stop, and restart replays both drained inputs with one history row per stable input key and one answer event.

## Requested checks

- **One coordinator for fatal and signal stops — CLOSED.** `src/core/container.ts:1113–1114` forwards both stale-epoch and fatal errors to `callbacks.onFatalStop`. `src/index.ts:34–40` supplies the callback calling `stopAndLeave('fatal core error', 1, error)`. SIGINT/SIGTERM at lines 256–262 go through `shutdown` to the same `stopAndLeave`, which invokes `runStopSequence`.
- **Second request / signal during a fatal stop — CLOSED.** In the third actual-entrypoint probe, the registry flush emitted a second fatal request through the installed `unhandledRejection` handler and sent an actual SIGTERM to the child while the first fatal stop was in flight. The controlled flush then settled after 60 ms. The child exited **1**, with exactly one coordinator-trigger log, one `Shutting down...` log and one registry flush. No second stop or hard-deadline error appeared. Observed fatal-log-to-exit interval: 87 ms. `stopAndLeave` sets its dedup flag synchronously before awaiting the sequence (`src/index.ts:248–253`), so the later requests cannot replace the first fatal exit status.
- **Hard exit armed before any awaited step — CLOSED.** In `src/index.ts`, arming at line 187 precedes the health-server close await (199), settings close await (214), and container shutdown await (220). An additional temporary process probe, `review-f8-early.test.ts` / `review-f8-early-child.ts`, called the actual exported `runStopSequence` with a settings close that never resolves. It recorded `CLOSE_ENTERED`, exited **1** with the hard-exit error, and never entered container shutdown. This independently checks that an early awaited close cannot prevent arming.
- **AGENTS.md sentence — CLOSED / true to the code.** Line 335 accurately describes this pre-turn normalization boundary. The normalization-error catch in CoreLoop marks the core stopped and returns before the snapshot commit; stop on that already-stopped loop does not commit the partial tick. The real entrypoint now supplies the bounded, non-zero process exit. The retained restart regression exercises replay of the whole drained batch and idempotent history writes. A permanently unchanged store rejection has no repair path in the stop coordinator: restart retries the durable input, so store repair remains necessary. The sentence does not weaken the existing bounded-stop guarantee.

## Mutation evidence — one non-blocking OPEN coverage comment

Both mutations were planted separately and fully restored.

| Mutation | Committed `fatal-stop-process.test.ts` | Independent actual-entrypoint probes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Restore the pre-fix container callbacks: each sets `process.exitCode = 1` and calls `void shutdown?.()` instead of forwarding `callbacks.onFatalStop` | **SURVIVED: both tests passed** | **KILLED:** clean and stalled cases timed out waiting for bounded fatal exit; duplicate-request case failed because the normalization fatal never entered the coordinator |
| Change `process.exit(code)` in `src/index.ts:223` to `process.exit(0)` | **KILLED:** clean fatal-stop test failed at line 43, expected 1, received 0; stalled test still passed through the independent hard-exit path | Not rerun for this mutation |

**OPEN, non-blocking: committed regression coverage does not protect the routing fix.** `tests/fixtures/fatal-stop-child.ts:43` calls `runStopSequence` directly. It bypasses both the callback registration in `main()` and the container's fatal callback forwarding. Consequently, the new process tests stay green with the exact old routing bug restored. They test the coordinator's behavior, not whether a real normalization failure reaches it. Recommended follow-up: retain an actual-entrypoint rejected-history-write process test, including a stalled stop and duplicate requests. The temporary probes above demonstrate a discriminating test approach.

This is a test-strength comment, not a currently broken lifemodel-avy.6 DONE WHEN, ADR-010 rule or AGENTS.md runtime guarantee. The original F8 correctness finding is CLOSED. Per the brief's blocking scope and the repository's mutation fallback policy, this survivor alone does not block acceptance. No tracker change was made; the coordinator can record this follow-up.

## Commands and results

All shell commands were sequential, without shell background operators or exit-hiding pipelines. Heavy commands used `lifemodel-heavy`. Exit codes below are the checked commands' own exit codes.

| Command / tree | Own exit | Files / tests |
| --- | ---: | --- |

The actual PostgreSQL trigger was dropped in probe cleanup; all test stores/processes belonged to disposable launcher runs. No host dependencies were installed. No tracker operation, test-VM action, commit or push occurred. No additional Nix, present-document or automatic document-transition check was run. title: A new generation takes over from the running one, and a broken one reverts itself
description:
Charter: docs/charters/instance-1.md, outcome 5, re-cut 2026-10-11 by the owner (lifemodel-he0; was "A broken version reverts itself, and the owner can boot any generation"). The existing loader, extended and moved into its own container (the only one with Docker access), starts each generation of lifemodel as its own container beside the running one, the way Kubernetes rolls out a stateless service: liveness and readiness probes, then the switch of the epoch, a health window after each switch (completed work, not a live process), self-healing to the previous healthy generation with a report, and the maintenance mode (entered by hand or after N consecutive failed generations) where the owner boots any generation. A generation keeps no state: Valkey holds the event bus (streams) and one current tick snapshot, committed atomically with the epoch check, fsync on every write; Postgres with pgvector holds memory and configuration; OpenBao, beside Agent Vault, issues credentials. The tick is the only boundary; a planned switch lets the old generation finish its tick and leave, the new continues from the snapshot. Reversible format migrations (expanding by preference; a breaking change carries an up/down pair and a format version, the down run before starting an older generation, the switch refused if it fails) and "refuse when uncertain" carry over from the replaced candidate-first design (lifemodel-b0r.2/.3/.8, documents in docs/features/instance/generations-*.md kept as its record). Open for design: health-window length and failure threshold, re-issuing a model request cut by a switch, the shape of "one command" with several containers. Greenfield: nothing to migrate.

## DONE WHEN
In the test environment the loader, in its own container, starts generation N+1 as a container beside N; N+1 passes its readiness probe and the epoch switches; the conversation continues from the current snapshot with no message lost or answered twice; a generation that never becomes healthy is replaced, without the owner, by the previous healthy one with a report; in the loader's maintenance mode the owner boots an older generation, and data changed by a breaking migration is brought back to that generation's format; outcome 4's check walked again on this shape (one command starts the instance, no key in lifemodel's process, panic holds across restarts).

comments.author: claude-code
comments.text: Owner decision, 2026-10-16: the check a new generation must pass before it takes over includes a real model turn through the egress gateway, on the model actually configured (a request, an answer and one tool call). A generation whose model client is broken never takes over; one that breaks later reverts (lifemodel-u8t). Reason: the model client is the one module lifemodel cannot repair without itself, so a broken one must never replace a working one. Model access configuration lives in the loader (decision on lifemodel-2t5).

title: Design container generations: loader-run containers, Valkey bus and tick snapshot, Postgres state
description:
Design stage of lifemodel-b0r on the owner's decision of 2026-10-11 (charter docs/charters/instance-1.md, "Generations as containers"; lifemodel-he0). Owner decisions are fixed inputs, not options: the existing loader (extended, not rewritten) in its own container, the only one with Docker, starts generation containers beside the running one with liveness/readiness probes, epoch switch, health window (completed work), rollback with a report, maintenance mode; Valkey holds the event bus (streams) and one current tick snapshot committed atomically with the epoch check (emitted events + snapshot with bus position), fsync on every write, periodic snapshot copies; Postgres with pgvector holds memory and configuration, no shared folder; OpenBao beside Agent Vault issues credentials; the tick is the only boundary, async results arrive on the bus; external actions run after the tick commits, from command events; planned switch = old finishes its tick and leaves, new continues from the current snapshot; greenfield; core not cut; replay, hot standby, functions, other languages later; web channel designed separately (lifemodel-vhd). Carried over: reversible format migrations (up/down, format version), refuse when uncertain.
Open for this design: how a generation gets its code (today a git repo on a volume, self-change = commit, no image rebuild); health window length and failure threshold; a model request cut by a switch; fencing writes to the bus; the shape of "one command" with several containers (outcome 4 re-walked); how OpenBao credentials reach a generation; what loader state lives where.
Method: docs/.. ADD (to-design design.md): drivers with measured quality scenarios, inventory of the existing code, at least two options from named patterns including one rejecting the shared assumption, MADR decision record (docs/adr/010-*.md, the next free number: 006-009 exist on branches), the views it turns on, review by a different model (openai-codex gpt-6.1-sol) before building, scenarios handed to to-stages as checks. Docs only: no product code, no runtime probes, no heavy CI.

## DONE WHEN
docs/adr/010 records the container-generations design (context, drivers with measured scenarios, considered options, decision, consequences, rejected options with reasons, assumptions with what invalidates them), the views it turns on are drawn, every open question above is decided or named as the owner's trade, a different-model review's blocking findings are resolved on the record, and the automatable scenarios are listed as checks for to-stages; merged to main by the owner.

comments.author: claude-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:main#6a3f2eb1
comments.text:
Owner review of ADR-010 (PR #28), point by point, 2026-10-12 - decisions so far, to be written into ADR-010 / design / charter in one pass after all 8 points:
1. Code: a generation = a commit. Modules are described by a Compose Specification subset in the repo (build context + Dockerfile per module; launch rights/flags are the loader's, never the file's). The loader builds each module image with docker build (BuildKit sandbox, no Docker access/credentials; normal network). Image tag = hash of the module's build inputs (git tree id of build context + additional_contexts); unchanged module = no build. Base images pinned by digest; no loader build args. Checks are a build stage. Whole generation switches together; per-module generations later. Replaces O1-A (sealed tree mount). Dev-machine limits (11 GB) are NOT design drivers: Q11 = measure and name the two-generation need.
2. Fencing: unchanged from ADR (epoch fencing token: Valkey CAS script + Postgres active_holder row; OpenBao revocation + connection kill at switch; no raw Valkey write commands).
3. Rollback/migrations: no down migrations. Expand/contract (parallel change); invariant "the predecessor reads everything I write", checked as a build-stage check; contract only in a later generation. Automatic rollback = previous healthy generation on CURRENT data. Snapshot copies = manual recovery in maintenance only. 2 consecutive failures -> maintenance; panic overrides. Charter outcome 5 check changes: the owner boots an older generation within the compatibility window; older ones refuse with the reason (drop "brought back by breaking migration").
4. In-flight work: the core makes no external calls - it writes command events; an executor module of the generation (same code/image, own entrypoint) runs them and writes results to the bus. Core drain = finish the current tick (switchDrainMs no longer 90 s). Old executor finishes its own jobs within a grace period (setting, ~300 s, to be measured), then the rest is re-run by the new executor with a report; job heartbeat + zombie re-run; jobs pinned to the version they were issued under. Long waits = suspended, no process held; completion arrives as a bus event. Side-effecting calls carry a key + "done" record (default: side-effecting = yes); web-chat reply = insert by key. Motor runs use the same mechanism. Bus events compatible both ways during a switch. File research "Windmill vs Temporal vs own executor" before designing outcome 6.
Remaining: points 5-8.

comments.author: claude-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:main#6a3f2eb1
comments.text: Owner review of ADR-010, point 5 (2026-10-12): state homes as in ADR (tick working state in the Valkey snapshot, inbound as a Valkey stream with offsets in the snapshot, long-lived memory/conversations/soul/registries/schedules/config in Postgres). Neurons are CORE plugins: they stay in the core process behind the plugin API for now; extracting them into isolated modules is later (options: sensor containers publishing to the bus / WASM sandbox in-core / one neuron-host process) - file as deferred; until then 'a neuron cannot crash the core' rests on error handling, not physical isolation. Feature plugins (calories, reminder, news, web-search, web-fetch) become function images (Nuclio-style) in this milestone, all five; their influence on the body = signals on the bus. A new or changed plugin goes only through a commit and a generation, no hot reload. Skills as instructions = data in Postgres. Postgres writes: keyed commands applied after the tick commit, epoch-checked, idempotent by natural keys (generic applied table only where none exists). Web-chat delivery proof = the message row itself. Remaining: points 6-8.

comments.author: claude-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:main#6a3f2eb1
comments.text: Owner review of ADR-010, point 6 (2026-10-12): static part = a Compose file (loader, Valkey, Postgres, OpenBao, Agent Vault, Caddy as separate containers, official images), one command = docker compose up -d; Docker restart policies replace the loader's re-adopt of infra. The loader creates only generations and modules through a Docker socket proxy. Generations/modules sit on an internal:true Docker network (replaces the iptables egress rule and NET_ADMIN); the only way out is OUR egress door module (per-module policy, logging, rate limits added there when needed), which calls Agent Vault for key injection. Modules talk only through the bus; language/process/machine are each module's business; the bus contract (event format, versions, keys) is the load-bearing standard. Light functions: workerd as the first, replaceable engine (ADR records why and what replacing takes): functions use only the WinterTC common API (lint-checked), engine config is generated from the Compose manifest by one engine driver in the loader, egress routing and bus I/O live outside the function (EIP Channel Adapter between Valkey and the function over HTTP). Taken now because the core will be split into ~30 modules. No multi-engine abstraction yet. Remaining: points 7-8.

comments.author: claude-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:main#6a3f2eb1
comments.text: Owner review of ADR-010, point 7 (2026-10-12): OpenBao issues short-lived Postgres and Valkey credentials per MODULE ROLE with least privilege (core: epoch-checked tick commit + pg apply; channel adapter/intake: append to their streams only; functions: none; door: Agent Vault only). Delivery = the envconsul model: each module container runs OpenBao Agent in Process Supervisor mode (env_template + exec), which injects credentials into the module's environment (not in docker inspect), renews leases, restarts the module only when a credential actually changes (max TTL in days, a setting). Secret zero: the loader gives each agent a single-use response-wrapped AppRole secret-id. At a switch the loader revokes the old generation's leases. Rule: a module does not start unvetted child processes inheriting its environment. Model keys stay behind Agent Vault via the door; unseal key loader-held. Remaining: point 8.

comments.author: claude-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:main#6a3f2eb1
comments.text: Owner review of ADR-010, point 8 (2026-10-12): no down migrations; expand/contract with Tolerant Reader. Bus contract = AsyncAPI + JSON Schema in the repo, FULL compatibility checked at build (both directions, since old and new read each other's events during a switch); a breaking change = a new event type published beside the old one for a while, the old removed by a later contract step. Tick snapshot carries a format version, additive fields, tolerant reader; a generation seeing a NEWER snapshot version refuses to start and reports why; 'predecessor reads my snapshot' checked at build. Postgres: one schema per module (CREATE SCHEMA), the module's OpenBao role has rights only on its schema; migrations expanding only, applied by the loader before the switch under a DDL role; a language-neutral plain-SQL migration tool (dbmate or Atlas), replaceable; contract migrations later, deprecated items marked. ALL 8 POINTS DECIDED - next: rewrite ADR-010 + design + checks, fresh different-model review, charter amendment, then the work plan.

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner simplification review of ADR-010, point 0 (2026-10-12): threat model. Module code is trusted against MALICE, not against BUGS (written by us or by lifemodel itself). We defend against a broken generation (crash, hang, corrupting data by mistake, writing what the predecessor cannot read), NOT against a module deliberately bypassing rules. Kept: cheap structural barriers against mistakes (loader control network, Docker proxy and Agent Vault physically unreachable from modules; per-module Postgres role on its own schema only; snapshot write through an epoch check). Dropped: defences against deliberate bypass (mTLS workload identity, Valkey module/commit gateway, grace capabilities). Invalidator: modules from foreign sources (third-party plugins) - then revisit. Next: points 1-6 one by one.

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner simplification review, point 1 (2026-10-12): the unit of replacement is the MODULE, not the generation (amends decision 1 'whole generation switches together'). Generation = commit = desired state (like a Deployment revision); the loader is a controller that replaces only modules whose image tag changed; unchanged modules are not touched. Per-module strategy from the Compose standard field deploy.update_config.order: start-first (RollingUpdate: new starts, passes readiness, joins its Valkey consumer group, old gets terminate and finishes within its grace = terminationGracePeriod, executor ~300 s) for modules whose writes are keyed (intake, executor, functions, adapter, door); stop-first (Recreate/StatefulSet: old finishes its tick, Docker confirms exit, new takes epoch + snapshot) for singleton state writers (today: the core only). Single host: confirmed container exit gives one writer; no Valkey module/commit gateway, no two-store epoch barrier; the Lua epoch check stays as a cheap guard against loader bugs. Invalidator: modules on several machines -> fencing returns. Changed modules are replaced ONE BY ONE in manifest order; a readiness failure stops the rollout and rolls back. Health window starts after all changed modules of the commit are replaced; rollback restores the previous commit's desired state (only changed modules go back). OpenBao leases are revoked when the old instance exits (closes R3-01). Mixed old/new modules rely on decision 8 (bus FULL compatibility, expand-only Postgres).

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner simplification review, point 2 (2026-10-12): executor jobs. A job = a keyed command event in a Valkey stream read through a consumer group; XACK only after the result is recorded; a dead executor's pending job is taken by another via XAUTOCLAIM (built-in, no own zombie takeover/state machine/job heartbeats). Done record by key checked before and written after the effect; crash between effect and done record: keyed destination -> retry (destination dedups), unkeyed -> 'uncertain', reported, not retried. Jobs issued by an older version are run by the new executor (bus FULL compatibility, decision 8); no retained-image runners. For the core everything is async (command event out, result event in). Waiting for an answer that arrives on its own (webhook, human reply, timer): send, record the correlation as ordinary state, ack, exit; the answer arrives on the bus - no special mechanism, done now. A call whose answer comes on the same connection (model HTTP call, page fetch, Motor run) is held by the executor (Half-Sync/Half-Async; the external protocol's fact). TIMEOUTS (Release It!): every sync call declares a timeout per destination in the module's call manifest (with its keyed/unkeyed class); a call without a declared timeout fails the build; the executor cuts the connection at the timeout; after a cut: keyed -> retry policy, unkeyed -> 'uncertain'; build check: executor grace >= the longest declared timeout; the egress door also enforces a per-request timeout. No unbounded sync calls. Windmill/Temporal research stays before outcome 6, not blocking this milestone.

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner simplification review, point 3 (2026-10-12): Docker networks instead of mTLS. Networks: modules (internal: all modules, Valkey, Postgres, OpenBao, egress gateway, loader as client only), egress (egress gateway only - the only internet route), vault (internal: egress gateway + Agent Vault), docker (internal: loader + Docker socket proxy), and one network per service behind Caddy: front-loader (Caddy + loader: boot.<host> UI and forward_auth session check), front-vault (Caddy + Agent Vault UI), front-web (Caddy + lifemodel web intake); only Caddy publishes a port. The loader answers only Caddy; on the modules network it is a client only. Module control: Docker lifecycle, Compose healthcheck, epoch key in Valkey writable only by the loader role (no /activate, /drain HTTP endpoints). mTLS workload identity DEFERRED to the backlog (return when modules span machines or come from foreign sources). Architecture rule: interactions are one-directional, acyclic, through the bus where possible; explicit exceptions: stores, Docker proxy, healthcheck, owner entry via Caddy, adapter<->workerd inside one function-host module. The 'door' is named EGRESS GATEWAY; it consumes 'external request' commands from the bus, runs them with timeouts, and puts results back on the bus; the requester identity = the stream it wrote to (Valkey ACL: a module writes only its own streams). Open next: is a separate executor still needed (amends decision 4).

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner simplification review, point 4 (2026-10-12): NO executor module (amends decision 4; the rest of decision 4 stands: core makes no external calls, keyed jobs, grace, re-run by key, both-ways event compatibility). Work goes to the module that owns it, each a bus consumer group under the point-2 rules (key, done record, XAUTOCLAIM, mandatory timeout) and replaced under point 1 (EIP Message Endpoint per capability, Competing Consumers): model calls - the core builds the request (src/llm/provider.ts) and puts an 'HTTP request' command (timeout, destination class) on the bus; the EGRESS GATEWAY performs it and returns the response as an event (no streaming today). Tools (web-search, web-fetch, news) - function host, their HTTP via egress gateway commands. Reply delivery and the owner's transcript - the INGRESS GATEWAY (web module: browser -> Caddy -> ingress gateway -> bus; browser pulls replies from it). Motor runs - own Motor module with its OWN narrow Docker socket proxy (option A: only create/start/stop/remove containers labelled motor, no host mounts, no privileges); the loader stays control-only. Grace = Compose stop_grace_period per module (gateway >= its longest call timeout, Motor >= its run limit). RULE: only two modules touch the world - ingress gateway and egress gateway; everything else only through the bus. Explicit exceptions: (a) Caddy is infrastructure in front of ingress; (b) Agent Vault is the last hop of the egress path (egress gateway -> Agent Vault -> internet; reachable only on the vault network); (c) Motor sandbox traffic goes through the egress gateway acting as an HTTP proxy (HTTPS_PROXY) with a motor policy, no own route out; (d) the loader's BuildKit builds use the network (decision 1), outside the rule, may later go via the gateway or a package mirror. Later Telegram: inbound via ingress (webhook) or egress (polling), sending via egress.

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner simplification review, point 5 (2026-10-12): compatibility is checked on SCHEMAS, not by running predecessor readers on data. Bus and snapshot: schemas in the repo (AsyncAPI for events, JSON Schema for the snapshot); FULL compatibility compares the schema files of the running commit and the candidate (Confluent Schema Registry style); snapshot version not bumped for additive fields. Postgres: expand-only migrations linted by squawk (MIT, plain SQL; bans drop/rename column or table, type change, NOT NULL without default); contract steps in a later commit. The check is bound to the COMMIT PAIR, not the image: the loader compares schema and migration files of running vs candidate commit at every rollout, even when all images are reused (closes R3-06 without admission records). Dropped: throwaway Postgres, predecessor-reader runs on candidate data, image-bound admission records. Rule: a column's meaning never changes; a new meaning = a new column (semantic changes are caught only by review and the health window). Migration tool: dbmate + squawk (closes open question 4).

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner simplification review, point 6 (2026-10-12): snapshot copies and backup. A snapshot copy is taken ONLY when the core is replaced (stop-first): by the loader right after the old core committed its last tick and exited (the point the new core starts from); other module replacements do not touch the snapshot. Keep the last N copies (setting, proposed 3) in Valkey beside the current snapshot. Restore from a copy is manual, maintenance mode only; the loader first checks the copy's snapshot schema is readable by the current core (point 5 schema rule) and that the copy's stream positions are not trimmed; otherwise it refuses with the reason. Postgres is NOT rolled back: the core continues on current data; re-applied commands are keyed. Full backup (Postgres dump + Valkey copy) only on the owner's command in maintenance mode, never part of a switch or rollback. Dropped: snapshot + Postgres stamp pair and its consistency rules. Backlog: automatic regular Postgres backups (outside this milestone).

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner simplification review, values (2026-10-12): core stop deadline (finish tick + commit snapshot) 5 s, then forced stop, unfinished tick re-run by key; stop_grace_period: egress gateway >= its longest call timeout (target 300 s, to measure), Motor >= Motor run limit, other modules 30 s; OpenBao lease max TTL 7 days; snapshot copies kept 3; health window 120 s, first-commit deadline 30 s, 2 consecutive failures -> maintenance (unchanged). All are loader settings or manifest fields. Next: rewrite ADR-010 from scratch on decisions 1-8 + simplification points 0-6 (removed mechanisms listed as rejected options), short gpt-6.1-sol review with the point-0 threat model given, charter amendment, work plan.

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner decision, platform (2026-10-12): move to k3s now instead of Docker/Compose ('better to switch to k3s now than suffer with Docker'). On a VM: install k3s, deploy via GitOps; into an existing cluster: Helm. NOT k3s inside Docker (no privileged container). Generation = commit = GitOps desired state; the GitOps controller applies changed modules one by one (RollingUpdate for keyed writers, Recreate/StatefulSet for the singleton core); rollback = revert the desired state in the deploy branch (only changed modules go back); panic = suspend sync + scale modules to zero. Delivery changes: images + a Helm chart; clean VM = k3s + GitOps bootstrap with one command; existing cluster = helm install; k3d only as dev/CI test environment. The loader becomes a GENERATION OPERATOR in the cluster (RBAC): sees a new lifemodel commit, runs checks and in-cluster BuildKit image builds (tag = build-input hash, local registry), writes new tags to the deploy branch, computes the completed-work health window, rolls back via git, maintenance mode, the owner's web UI/login/panic. Choices (owner agreed to the recommendations): Flux (HelmRelease, image automation; no own UI needed); our operator does health analysis and rollback (Flagger/Argo Rollouts do not cover the singleton core); Postgres via CloudNativePG operator (pgvector, declarative roles, backups); Traefik (bundled with k3s, ForwardAuth replaces Caddy forward_auth). OpenBao via its official Helm chart with Agent Injector and Kubernetes auth (service account login replaces wrapped AppRole secret-ids). Isolation: NetworkPolicy (default-deny egress; only the egress gateway goes out); Motor gets RBAC rights only on Jobs in its own namespace (no Docker access at all). Unchanged: threat model, bus/jobs rules, timeouts, schema compatibility, function host, ingress/egress-only rule, snapshot copies, values. Next: rewrite ADR-010 on k3s/GitOps (third rewrite), review, then charter amendment and plan anew.

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner decision, credentials on k8s (2026-10-12, R5-04): use the Bank-Vaults secrets webhook (bank-vaults/secrets-webhook, Apache 2.0) with OpenBao - the owner runs this exact setup in their own cluster, OpenBao supported. Mechanism: the mutating webhook adds an init container that copies vault-env into a shared volume and wraps the container command; vault-env logs in with Kubernetes auth (service account), resolves secret references into environment variables, execs the module process; secrets not in the pod spec, Kubernetes Secrets or etcd; the token is flushed before the app starts. Daemon mode: vault-env stays the parent, renews dynamic Postgres/Valkey leases; on renewal failure the process exits and Kubernetes restarts it (= restart on change, decision 7 kept). No agent baked into images; works for modules in any language. Replaces the OpenBao Agent Injector in the k3s ADR. Verify in implementation: daemon-mode renewal of dynamic Postgres/Valkey credentials and clean exit on failure.

comments.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-13 (platform delivery, after 'Почему установщик? Установщик ставит только loader' and 'почему не развертывать кластер через gitops сразу?'): (1) The cluster is deployed by GitOps from the first second. The one command on a clean VM installs k3s, Flux and ONE source: an OCIRepository pointing at the signed platform release artifact CI publishes (cosign-verified). Flux installs the whole PLATFORM layer from it: the loader (generation operator), Gitea, OpenBao and its webhook, CNPG, Agent Vault, registry, policies. lifemodel cannot write that source; a platform upgrade is a version change on the owner's command. Gitea is platform, outside generations, under GitOps from the release. No installer-owned Helm releases, no installer custody of credentials. (3) This milestone delivers ONLY a dedicated VM ('Нужна просто отдельная ВМ'); installing into an existing cluster is a separate deferred feature: the owner would not let Flux or cluster-wide objects into their own cluster; the approach there is the usual chart toggles - each platform dependency can be disabled and replaced by an external one (e.g. openbao.enabled=false requires an external OpenBao), inside lifemodel's own namespace with its operator.

comments.text: Decision (owner, 2026-10-07, after two review rounds on stage 1 kept finding shutdown races): the guarantee moves from the graceful handoff to a durable inbound log with Kafka-like semantics (owner: 'нужна очередь, что-то типа kafka'): append-only log of inbound messages written on receipt; a committed offset advances only after the answer is delivered; replay from the last committed offset at start; dedup by Telegram update_id. The stop becomes best effort: intake stop, drain up to 90 s, then a hard process exit at the deadline; internal signals are not persisted (regenerated by ticks). A crash (kill -9, OOM, broken generation) is best effort: the inbound log stays in its simple form (written on receipt, removed when the message's turn reached a recorded outcome: answered, deliberately silent, failed send or failed turn; no automatic retry of a failed outcome; replayed after start only when no outcome was recorded). Per-send delivery tracking and delivery evidence are removed. Rare crash windows are documented as known and filed as one debt item, not fixed in this run. Review stopping rule: only what breaks a graceful restart or is likely in real use blocks acceptance. Owner: 'Если это станет проблемой когда-нибудь, тогда и будем решать'. Valkey considered and rejected (same durability trade-off plus a service).

title: Simplify the stop on top of the log: remove the signal journal, bounded drain, hard exit at the deadline
description:
Built on lifemodel-ctc.2.1 (the log carries the guarantee). Remove the pending-signal journal (src/core/pending-signal-journal.ts and its restore/persist wiring) and the patches that only served it; keep the intake/full channel stop split and the awaited sends. The stop: stopIntake, drain the turn in flight and its sends up to the one deadline (default 90 s), then exit the process hard at the deadline whatever still hangs (hung send, stalled getUpdates, stalled tick). Idempotent shutdown stays. Docs (AGENTS.md, docs/architecture.md) say exactly what is guaranteed: messages via the log; internal signals are not persisted. TDD.

## DONE WHEN
A stop with a hung send, a stalled intake stop or a stalled tick ends within the deadline (hard exit); after restart every message is answered once via the log; the journal code is gone; typecheck, lint, full suite green.

title: Durable inbound log with a committed offset (Kafka-like), replay at start, update_id dedup
description:
Design (owner decision 2026-10-07, see the decision log on lifemodel-ctc): an append-only log of inbound user messages in core, written on receipt and flushed at once through DeferredStorage -> JSONStorage (AGENTS.md lesson 4); each entry has its Telegram update_id, recipient and signal. The consumer offset (per recipient or global, decide and justify) is committed only when the answer to that message is DELIVERED (send success), not when a turn starts or ends; a turn that absorbs messages commits them together with its answer. At start: replay uncommitted entries in order as signals; drop an update_id already in the log. Committed entries are compacted (kept bounded). Plugin Isolation: the channel only emits signals through its existing callback; the log lives in core. Also: channel.stopIntake must not lose a message whose handler is still running (photo handler awaits downloads): either wait for in-flight handlers within the deadline or the message reaches the log at emit time. TDD.

## DONE WHEN
The stage 2 criterion holds, with tests for each listed scenario; typecheck, lint, full suite green.

title: Run typecheck, lint and tests in CI
description:
CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs only the backlog checks today. The product checks — npm run
typecheck, npm run lint, npm run test — are missing from it.

Found during the shady2k-skills setup; filed with it. Adopted by lifemodel-ggc (self-change-1 outcome 3), stage lifemodel-ggc.1.

## Change (short spec delta, owner-approved preflight 2026-10-08)
1. package.json gets `check`: typecheck, lint, format:check, then `vitest run --maxWorkers=2`, stopping at the first failure with its exit code. AGENTS.md's Commands table lists it.
2. The two files on main that fail `npm run format:check` (domain-trackers.ts, status-update-service.ts) are formatted (a repair the merge waits on).
3. A classifier script under scripts/ reads changed paths (one per line) and answers whether product checks are owed. Not product: `.beads/**`, `docs/**`, `*.md` at the repository root, `.backlog/**`, `.githooks/*`, `scripts/connect-clone.sh`. Everything else is product (including .github/, package*.json, src/**/*.md, the classifier itself). An empty list is product (an empty diff is no evidence of safety).
4. ci.yml: a `changes` job runs the classifier on the PR's merge-base...head diff, or on a push's before..after diff (a missing or all-zero `before` means product). A `ci-product` job needs it, runs only when product is owed and the PR is not a draft: checkout, setup-node 24 with npm cache, `npm ci`, `npm run check`. `ci-backlog` is unchanged.
5. AGENTS.md and docs/backlog-integration.md (Full stage checks, CI, the hooks paragraph that says CI will be the product checks' home) describe the result; the ci.yml header comment too.

## Scenarios
- `npm run check` on a clean tree exits 0; a planted type error, lint error, formatting slip or failing test each makes it exit non-zero.
- classifier: [docs/x.md] -> no; [README.md] -> no; [.beads/issues.jsonl, AGENTS.md] -> no; [src/a.ts] -> yes; [docs/x.md, package.json] -> yes; [src/runtime/builtin-skills/s/SKILL.md] -> yes; [.github/workflows/ci.yml] -> yes; [] -> yes.

DONE WHEN: a CI job runs typecheck, lint and the vitest suite on pull requests and pushes to main,
with node 24 and npm ci; a change that cannot touch product code does not owe them.

title: A task's profile is set by the agent, a task asks for more access, and the platform holds the owner's ceilings
description:
Charter motor-1, outcome 3 (agreed 2026-10-19; owner decisions on lifemodel-653). The agent assigns each task its profile (files, domains, memory, CPU, time). A task that lacks something requests access instead of failing; the agent approves within the owner's ceilings, and asks the owner when it is unsure or the task is the owner's own commission. The platform enforces the ceilings, set in the loader's settings (memory, time, concurrent tasks, never-allowed domains); cluster-internal addresses and other tasks' files are always denied. A request beyond the ceilings reaches the owner as an ordinary lifemodel reply; the grant takes effect only after the owner's consent and is checked by the platform, not the model. Network: per-task egress only through the egress gateway (taken from lifemodel-2t5 for this milestone).

## DONE WHEN
On the test VM: a task without a domain in its profile cannot reach it, and normally reaches an allowed one through the egress gateway with no key in the task; a task's access request within the ceilings is granted by the agent and the running task then reaches the domain; a request beyond the ceilings is asked of the owner in the chat, refused until the owner agrees and granted after; a profile over a ceiling is refused by the platform even when the agent asks for it; a task over its memory or time limit is stopped.

Left out: the rest of lifemodel-2t5 (per-module store credentials, the Gitea admin Secret retirement).

title: The loader's Kubernetes custody client puts API response bodies into error messages, which bootstrap logs
description:
Found by review T5114-02 of lifemodel-s9v5.1.4 (2026-10-18), pre-existing on main. loader/src/openbao.ts (createKubernetesBaoCustody, ~239-271) concatenates the Kubernetes API error response body into thrown error messages, and the platform bootstrap logs the error description (loader/src/app.ts ~149-150). A Kubernetes error body that reflects request content or credential material can reach the loader's logs. The raw JSON-decode and transport-error paths are not sanitised either. The new role-parameterised OpenBao client is not affected (its typed errors carry no body).

What happens: a custody call fails with a body; the body text appears in the loader log. Should: errors carry only a safe operation name and status code. Breaks: AGENTS.md 'logs never carry credentials'; ADR-013's no-body error rule as applied to the loader.

DONE WHEN: every custody error is a safe code (operation + status) with no response body or raw transport/parse message; a recording-logger test with a secret-bearing synthetic Kubernetes error body (4xx, 5xx, malformed JSON, transport error) finds no part of the body in any error message or log line, and normally a custody failure still names its operation.

Left out: the OpenBao client itself (already covered by lifemodel-s9v5.1.4).

title: A task works on a git repository — lifemodel itself, a new project or the owner's existing one — in by a bundle, out by a verified push and pull request, holding no key
description:
Owner, 2026-10-21: asked how a git repository reaches a task, how its commits come back and how Motor
Cortex updates itself; agreed («Да») to the direction below, and added: «мы же пишем код не только для
себя. Я могу попросить агента написать что-то новое или исправить имеющийся проект.»

So a task works on one of three kinds of repository: lifemodel itself (self-change), a new project, or an
existing project of the owner's elsewhere (e.g. GitHub). Constraints already decided: the task holds no
key at all (ADR-014 T03); external effects need a current exact-scope grant (ey3e); a trusted platform
service accepts an approved immutable change, never arbitrary git transport with reusable credentials
(tasks-options.md).

Direction (agreed):
- **In:** before the harness starts, a platform init step places a `git bundle` of the requested commit in
  the task's working volume; the task clones from the local file — no network, no key, exactly that
  commit. Source: the internal Gitea (lifemodel, new projects), or an external remote fetched by the
  platform through the egress gateway with a read credential held in OpenBao (public repos need none).
- **Out:** the task makes `git bundle create` of its branch, uploads it with `lifemodel-storage` and marks
  it an artifact (all of this exists after stage 2). A trusted push service verifies it (descends from
  the given base commit, only refs `task/<id>`, size bound), then — after the owner's grant for an
  external remote — pushes the branch and opens a pull request through the host's API, with a push
  credential that never leaves the platform. A new project is created as a repository in the internal
  Gitea; publishing it elsewhere (e.g. Gitea's push mirror) is a separate granted action.
- **Self-update of Motor Cortex:** the harness version is pinned in the workbench Dockerfile; an update is
  an ordinary commit (possibly a self-change task's PR) and a generation; new tasks take the new image
  digest, a running task keeps the digest snapshotted at acceptance. Nothing updates itself in place.

Questions to settle when picked up: which external hosts first (GitHub's API for PRs; plain git remotes
without PRs); how the owner connects a remote and its credentials (loader settings, OpenBao); private
submodules and LFS; the bundle size bound.

Not in motor-1. Feature title only until planned.

## DONE WHEN
On the test VM the owner asks the agent to fix a bug in an existing GitHub repository of theirs and
separately to start a new project; each task works from a bundle, the fix arrives as a pull request on
GitHub after the owner approves it, the new project appears in the internal Gitea; no task spec, env,
file or log holds any git credential.

title: A reply in the web chat appears without a page reload, also when the event stream was refused or ended
description:
Owner 2026-10-19 on the test VM (web from main 1ca860e, loader/gateway from a883b4a, a real opencode go model): "чат стал отвечать. Но я почему-то не увидел ответ сразу, только после перезагрузки страницы". Finding 2 of 8 in motor-1 (the conversation, outcome lifemodel-hf2k).

What a person does: sends a message in the web chat. What happens: the reply does not appear; it appears after reloading the page. Expected: the reply appears live through /api/events without a reload, and a broken or refused stream recovers by itself.

Coordinator's first look (not proven): src/web/server.ts /api/events answers 429 too_many_streams / 503 stream_unavailable when a stream lease is still held (MAX_STREAMS_PER_SESSION, transcript stream lease) — a browser EventSource treats any non-200 answer as fatal and never reconnects (web/app/src/transport.ts subscribe has no error handling or resubscribe). Other candidates: the stream's max age (STREAM_MAX_AGE_MS) ending it before a slow real-model reply, a lease left by a previous tab or the restart, proxy buffering. Reproduce first; the real model answered after many seconds.

## DONE WHEN
A reply committed while the page is open appears without a reload, also when the reply takes longer than a minute, after the event stream was ended or refused once (429/503/network), and after a web module restart; checked through the real web server and a real browser test; and normally an open page receives each reply exactly once.

comments.author: claude-code-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:main#d388c27e
comments.text: Owner 2026-10-19: "Если я вышел, то меня нужно перенаправить на страницу авторизации" (not a 'no connection' line). Mechanism found: loader/src/http.ts /_auth/verify answers a GET without a session with a redirect to the login page (next = the page's URI); a non-GET gets 401; a loader that is down gives the proxy's own error (5xx). So: when the page's catch-up read (fetch with redirect:'manual' → an opaqueredirect, or a 401) shows the session is gone, the page saves its unsent draft (sessionStorage), navigates the top window to its own URL so the loader's redirect takes it to login and back, and restores the draft on return; a 5xx or network failure (loader rollout) keeps retrying silently.

title: The platform installs only the Flux controllers it uses, so a 2-vCPU node has CPU room for workload rollouts
description:
Found by the lifemodel-vhd acceptance walk (2026-10-16) on the 2-vCPU test VM: the platform installs Flux from the upstream `install.yaml` (deploy/nixos/default.nix, scripts/install.sh), which brings all seven controllers, 650m of CPU requests. The platform uses source, kustomize, helm, notification and source-watcher; image-reflector-controller and image-automation-controller (100m each, 1 Gi limit each) are unused (no ImageRepository/ImagePolicy/ImageUpdateAutomation anywhere). With the core at 750m the node sits at 1950m of 2000m requested, so a one-replica web rollout (maxSurge 1) fits only because the web request was cut to 50m (PR #46) — zero margin, and any new workload will not schedule.

## DONE WHEN
The NixOS module and the installer install only the Flux controllers the platform uses (a pinned, checksummed component set rather than the full install.yaml), a test asserts the installed set, and on the test VM from a clean snapshot the node's requested CPU drops by at least 200m with every Kustomization Ready. Normally the platform still reconciles every source it does today.

title: An npm ci in any worktree silently turns off the backlog and commit-link hooks in every checkout
description:
Found during setup 0.46.0 (lifemodel-1tsp), 2026-10-18. core.hooksPath lives in the repository's shared config. npm run connect sets it to .githooks; husky's prepare (run by npm ci in some worktree) resets it to .husky/_, a directory that exists only where npm ci ran. Every other checkout and worktree then has a hooksPath that does not exist, and git runs NO hook there: commits went in without the gate, the commit-link check or the product-document check, with no message. Found on the main checkout and the run's worktrees; repaired by rerunning npm run connect.

What should happen: hooks run in every checkout whether or not npm ci ran there, or a commit is refused saying to connect. Breaks: the installation's commit-link and gate enforcement (CI still enforces them).

DONE WHEN: after npm ci in one worktree, a commit in another checkout still runs the gate and the commit-link check (proved through the real entry points); and normally npm ci's own product hooks still run where node_modules exists.

title: Twenty-three npm advisories on main's lockfile are triaged and the ones reaching a shipped image are fixed
description:
Seen 2026-10-23 by the lifemodel-653.8.10 worker: `npm ci --ignore-scripts` on main's lockfile reported 23 dependency advisories (4 low, 6 moderate, 9 high, 4 critical). No dependency was changed in that work; nobody has read which packages they are, whether they reach shipped images (core, web, loader, workbench) or only dev tooling, and whether fixed versions exist.

What a person does: runs `npm ci` / builds an image. What happens: known-vulnerable packages may ship in an image. What should happen: each advisory is triaged — reachable in a shipped image or dev-only — and the reachable ones are upgraded or explicitly accepted with a reason.

## DONE WHEN
A triage list of the 23 advisories (package, path, severity, shipped image or dev-only, fix available); reachable high/critical ones upgraded with the full check green, or each accepted with a written reason; a recurring check decided (CI `npm audit` gate or the upkeep cadence).

Left out: changing the dependency policy or replacing packages beyond what the fixes need.

title: The NixOS module installs k3s, a pinned Flux and the verified root platform source, and nothing else
description:

title: The keyless identity patterns in the NixOS module and the script are anchored and escaped exactly as release.yml verifies them
description:
Stage lifemodel-lut.3. Defect against ADR-010 R7-06 found by the lifemodel-lut.2.3 worker: the NixOS module default (deploy/nixos/default.nix verify.subjectRegex, verify.issuer), scripts/install.sh defaults and the keyless fixture use UNANCHORED, UNESCAPED patterns ("https://github.com/shady2k/lifemodel/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v.*"); cosign/Flux match these as regular expressions searching a substring, so the check is looser than the ADR's single identity (issuer ^https://token\.actions\.githubusercontent\.com$, subject ^https://github\.com/shady2k/lifemodel/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@refs/tags/v.*$), which release.yml already verifies with. Make all three use exactly the ADR strings from one place, and add a check that the module default, the script default and release.yml agree byte for byte.

## DONE WHEN
nix flake check passes with fixtures carrying the anchored, escaped issuer and subject; a check fails if the module default, the script default and release.yml's verify identity differ.

title: CI runs the platform's real Kustomize render check, so a broken platform resource list cannot merge green
description:
Review finding L-06 (comment, gpt-6.1-sol, lifemodel-lut stage review 2026-10-13): the real Kustomize render of deploy/platform (parent and ./a0, with a negative case for a missing resource reference) and the other platform checks run in `nix flake check`, but CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) does not run `nix flake check`, and the isolated test launcher has no kustomize; so a broken platform resource list can merge with CI green. Fix: run `nix flake check` in CI (a job with Nix installed, pinned action, read-only permissions) or provision kustomize in the isolated boundary. Needs the owner's yes: it widens CI (a new job / a new tool in the boundary).

## DONE WHEN
A pull request that removes a resource from deploy/platform/a0/kustomization.yaml fails a required CI check.

title: The model gateway accepts a plain-text answer whose tool_calls is null, so a converting OpenAI-compatible endpoint can answer the chat
description:
Owner report 2026-10-19 on the test VM: after switching the primary slot to gpt-6-luna behind the owner's converting proxy (Chat Completions to Responses), every chat turn failed: 'Нет связи с моделью — сервер ответил неожиданно'; gateway log code bad_response.

Cause (coordinator probe in the gateway pod, owner-approved, shape only): the upstream answers a text reply as message {role, content: string, reasoning_content: null, tool_calls: null}. validateResponse (loader/src/model-gateway-response.ts) accepts tool_calls only when absent or an array, so null fails; the stream path's validateDelta has the same rule. Tool-call answers pass. Null is a common OpenAI-compatible encoding of 'no tool calls'.

Second defect, same area: when the primary fails and no reserve slot is set, the gateway logs and reports the failure under slot 'reserve' (activeSlot moves to 'reserve' before the absent read breaks the loop), so the owner is told about a slot they never configured. The failure must be attributed to the slot that failed.

Also seen: a request without tools made the same upstream return a 1.6 MB message.images entry; that is over MAX_BODY and is not this task (record only; the core always sends tools).

## DONE WHEN
Through the gateway: an upstream text answer with tool_calls: null (non-stream) and a stream delta with tool_calls: null reach the caller as answers; a non-array, non-null tool_calls still fails with bad_response. With the primary failing and no reserve, the log line and /status name slot primary; with a reserve configured and failing, they name reserve.

title: Modules reach Valkey and Postgres through a storage service instead of a shared code library
description: Idea from the lifemodel-vhd design (owner, 2026-10-15). Today modules use a shared code-level storage abstraction of domain operations (ADR-011 D4, O4-A); a storage service in front of Valkey and Postgres (O4-C) was kept as an idea. Triggers to take it up: a module written in another language (the charter's later Go/Rust), or the need for one access-control and audit point for all data. Cost to weigh then: a network hop on every core tick, a single point of failure, and moving the core's atomic epoch-checked snapshot commit into the service. Review date: when instance-1 closes.

title: The loader's OpenBao login fails on the standby redirect right after an unseal and waits a full retry
description:
Seen on the test VM walk (2026-10-14 07:11Z): after openbao-0 restarted and the loader unsealed it, the loader's POST auth/kubernetes/login got HTTP 307 (OpenBao redirects while the node is not yet active in HA mode) and the bootstrap loop logged a failure, recovering 30 s later. The loader treats the redirect as an error. Harmless today (one 30 s delay); it would matter where the loader's identity is needed promptly after a restart.

DONE WHEN: a login answered with 307 during the standby window is retried promptly (or the redirect followed to the active node) without logging a bootstrap failure; a test covers it.

title: A new version replaces the running one without losing the conversation
description:
Charter: docs/charters/platform-1.md, outcome 1. Design: ADR-006 stage 1 (loader, immutable generations, blue/green cutover: standby, readiness, drain, lease handoff). The rollout is a loader command; who issues it (the owner, a deploy script, later the agent via core.generation) is not part of the outcome. Includes the one dialogue piece the charter keeps: stop/cutover finishes or requeues the cognition turn in flight instead of losing it.

## DONE WHEN
In the development test environment, a loader command brings up a new generation beside the running one; the measured switch gap is at most 2 s, and no Telegram update is lost or handled twice across the switch.

title: The model gateway's first-byte timeout test times out at random in the full check and can turn main red
description:
Seen 2026-10-23 on main's CI after PR #116 merged (Actions run 39887951130, ci-product, attempt 1): `tests/unit/model-gateway.test.ts` "switches on the first-byte timeout and aborts the old request" (line 598) ran into Vitest's 5 s test timeout (5002 ms); 290 of 291 files passed. Neither the test nor `loader/src/model-gateway*.ts` changed since 2026-10-19, and the merged change did not touch them. Third random full-check failure in a day (with lifemodel-653.7.11 and lifemodel-653.8.1), each making a green main red.

What a person does: merges or pushes to main, or runs `npm run check`. What happens: rarely, this test times out. What should happen: it waits for the abort event it checks (the old request's `close`) with a deadline of its own and passes under the other Vitest worker's load.

DONE WHEN: reproduced under load (the file alongside a CPU-heavy concurrent file, several runs), the cause named (first-byte timer of 35 ms against a test-wide 5 s budget, or the latch never resolving), the test waits on the event, 5 of 5 under that load, and it still fails when the old request is not aborted (mutation).

Deferred: the motor-1 finding budget (8) is spent; owner decision needed to admit it.

title: A commit becomes a generation: changed modules are built in the cluster and replaced one by one
description:
Outcome 5, feature 5 of 7. ADR-010 Q1/Q2/Q8: the operator polls main in Gitea, runs the compatibility checks inside an in-cluster BuildKit build (tag = build-input hash, local registry), writes the deploy branch step by step, Flux replaces the changed modules one by one (RollingUpdate for keyed writers, one-replica StatefulSet for the core with the epoch switch). Checks F1, F2, F3, F6, Q1, Q12, N-1..N-6, N-12, N-13, N-17, N-22, G1, G2.

## DONE WHEN
A commit changing one module builds exactly one image and replaces only that module after its readiness; a core change switches the epoch and the conversation continues from the snapshot with no message lost or answered twice; a schema-breaking commit is refused before any image or pod exists.

title: The local zot registry serves its pushes and the node's pulls over TLS from the loader's CA
description:
Owner decision 2026-10-19 ('Давай сейчас zot по паролю, но потом TLS'): pwe ships zot on plain HTTP on the node address with password-authenticated push; TLS comes after.

Criterion: zot listens with a certificate issued by the loader's CA; k3s registries.yaml trusts that CA for the registry endpoint; BuildKit pushes and the kubelet pulls over TLS; a plain-HTTP pull or push is refused, and normally a generation build and pull succeed.

Left out: mTLS between modules (deferred by the owner 2026-10-12, ADR-010 O2-E).

title: A new question whose right answer equals the last reply gets no reply (duplicate-send guard)
description: Found by review 4 of lifemodel-ctc.2 (finding 2). The duplicate-send guard in src/core/intent-applicator.ts (~328-345) skips any SEND_MESSAGE whose text equals the last assistant message, including an answer to a new inbound question; the user gets nothing. Pre-existing behaviour (before lifemodel-ctc), restored unchanged by its rework. Likely fix: apply the guard only to proactive sends that answer no inbound message.
